## 10. Uniform critical and short-source recovery

The uncut first-gradient estimate pays the inherited critical-target certificate and gives

\[
\limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}
 m^2\|\mathsf C^\varepsilon\|_\infty
\le C(qr)^{257/256}
\]

on the retained schedule.

The inherited same-segment comparison gives

\[
|R_H^\varepsilon(t)-T_H^\varepsilon(t)|
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_{t-\delta}^{t+\delta}v^0(u)\,du,
\]

and the uniform \(v^0\) estimate yields

\[
\limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}
 m^2\|R_H^\varepsilon-T_H^\varepsilon\|_\infty
\le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\delta.
\]

The target selector is held at the target roof and is not differentiated. If one physical endpoint is grazing, the corresponding optical trace is zero and the selected source is controlled. A backward critical trace may be nonzero and is correctly retained.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 11. The unchanged decisive obstruction
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 11. The unchanged decisive obstruction

The final scalar inequality is

\[
\mathcal E_M
\le
\mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon(B)})
+C_MB^{-1/192}
+C(qr)^{257/256}
+C(1+\varepsilon(B)^{-1})qr,
\]

where

\[
q=\frac18,
\qquad
r=c\varepsilon(B)^4,
\qquad
a=\sqrt{qr},
\qquad
\delta=6qr.
\]

The explicit terms vanish as \(B\to\infty\). The remaining positive height

\[
\mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon(B)})
\]

has not been proved to vanish, even for one fixed radius.

Here \(T_{\mathsf S}^\varepsilon\) is the same-segment minimum of two original weighted physical endpoint traces, taken before physical sheets are summed. It is not the Jordan positive part of an already projected signed current.

The following facts do not control it:

1. small volume mass of the short source;
2. small difference between outgoing and incoming traces;
3. bounded geometric pressure;
4. cancellation of a projected signed forcing;
5. one-sheet Hölder regularity without a summable transverse capacity; or
6. vanishing of a trace only at genuinely grazing endpoints.

Two large positive traces can have a small difference. A positive density can retain large essential height on a roof interval of small mass. The positive common part can therefore carry the entire remaining upper spike.

A successful theorem must control the physically summed positive trace in the original normalized essential-height topology, or supply a bounded-overlap/capacity result strong enough to sum sheetwise estimates. An estimate of the form

\[
\mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon})
\le C_M\varepsilon^{-Q}\delta^\beta,
\qquad \beta>0,
\]

would be sufficient only after an explicit check that the retained or rebalanced outer schedule makes the right side vanish.

all_original_sections.original_text:
## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revision 102 is an actual theorem-bearing author revision. It repairs the submission-state defect identified in the revision-101 report: both named author branches point to the same new author commit, the active manuscript directory exists, and the packet contains a new article, three new proof modules, a source manifest, an itemized response and a dedicated exact-SHA workflow.

The mathematical response is also genuine. Revision 100 had reduced the unresolved upper pointwise problem to the positive same-segment minimum of two physical endpoint traces. That quantity could remain large even when the outgoing-minus-incoming trace difference and the associated volume source were small. Revision 102 now acts on this **positive minimum itself**. It introduces the barycentric representation

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon
 =c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)\,d\theta\,ds,
 \qquad
 \mathscr F(\theta,s)=a(\theta)+s\ell(\theta),
\]

where

\[
 c^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\min\{f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta),f^\varepsilon(b-,\theta)\}.
\]

It then uses the transverse field

\[
 V^\perp=(\partial_\theta\mathscr F)^{-1}\partial_\theta
\]

on regular pairing chambers, computes the paired-measure Jacobian, and proves a finite-count capped-clock comparison for the positive admitted source after physical sheets have been summed. Under the inherited schedule, the admitted source has normalized essential height

\[
 O(B^{-1/384}).
\]

This is substantive progress. It is not merely a renamed trace-difference estimate, a volume collar, a signed Jordan component or an averaged version of the target.

I audited the new modules

- `core/244_barycentric_positive_trace_coarea.tex`;
- `core/245_transverse_clock_and_pointwise_trace_height.tex`;
- `core/246_transverse_certificates_and_scalar_schedule.tex`;

and their dependence on the focused inputs, the revision-100 report, the response, the proof ledger, the source manifest and the principal pointwise target. Within the stated admitted scope, I found no decisive sign error, missing factor of the segment length, reversed transverse speed, exponent error, illegal collision-dependent cutoff, or hidden word-count factor.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the new argument. The scalar theorem is now

\[
 \mathcal E_M
 \le \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)+C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

where \(\mathsf U_B\) is the complete positive paired source on which the transverse clock fails. The manuscript explicitly retains in \(\mathsf U_B\):

- zero transverse speed;
- insufficient one-sided transverse reach;
- actual loss of pairing regularity;
- nonregular pairing strata carrying positive paired mass;
- uncontrolled logarithmic variation of the residence, paired weight or speed;
- folds of the endpoint roof maps; and
- positive backward-critical traces which are not admitted near the critical corner.

No estimate proves

\[
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\longrightarrow0.
\]

Indeed the manuscript proves that, along the unchanged outer schedule, the original pointwise theorem is equivalent to this limit. Thus the unresolved failure source is not a secondary remainder after the principal theorem. It is exactly the remaining upper obstruction.

The conditional certificate in module 246 is useful, but it is not verified uniformly on the complete physical pairing family. It gives a sufficient local criterion, not a theorem that the complement of the criterion has small mass or small essential height. The failure source could still carry the entire upper spike allowed by the previous reduction.

Consequently revision 102 does not prove the upper pointwise half, the unrestricted exact-label raw local limit theorem, or the unrestricted point-conditioned consequences organized by that theorem. At the requested benchmark, replacing one explicit positive source by a smaller explicit positive source is valuable progress but not closure of the governing result.

## 5. The inherited obstruction

Revision 100 had established, subject to its inherited inputs and its new geometric pressure theorem, a scalar reduction of the form

\[
 \mathcal E_M
 \le
 \mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon(B)})
 +C_MB^{-1/192}
 +C(qr)^{257/256}
 +C(1+\varepsilon(B)^{-1})qr.
\]

Here \(T_{\mathsf S}^\varepsilon\) is the positive minimum of the two original weighted endpoint traces on each selected short physical segment. The previous report emphasized that this is not the positive part of a projected signed current. Both endpoint traces can be large and almost equal, so their difference can be small while their minimum has a pointwise spike.

The revision-100 report asked for a theorem controlling that positive minimum itself, after physical summation or with a proved bounded-overlap theorem, at a rate compatible with the outer schedule.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 6. Regular pairing chambers
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 6. Regular pairing chambers

Module 244 fixes collision count, radius and exact label. It uses the finite physical graph, the exact section decisions and the retained endpoint-momentum injectivity to decompose the original paired measure into angular chambers on which the two roof endpoints

\[
 a(\theta),\qquad b(\theta)
\]

are \(C^2\), and the positive paired trace

\[
 c^\varepsilon(\theta)
\]

is locally Lipschitz.

At fixed collision count, definable cell decomposition can provide finitely many such intervals after further subdivision. The manuscript does not claim a collision-uniform bound on their number or derivatives. That restraint is appropriate: the subsequent positive coarea argument does not multiply by the number of chambers.

The treatment of chamber subdivision points is also structurally reasonable. They form a transverse-null set in \(\theta\), hence have zero mass for

\[
 c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)\,d\theta\,ds.
\]

Compatible Borel seams are assignments rather than new physical copies, and actual loss of regularity is put into the failure source rather than silently removed.

The most delicate part of this lemma is the asserted local Lipschitz regularity of the endpoint trace at a backward-critical entrance, where the trace need not vanish. The proof invokes the positive endpoint Hessian, a local inverse in the momentum variable, a lower tangential Hessian factor and the ordinary optical density. This is plausible in the declared physical coordinates, but it is compressed relative to its importance. A specialist should reconstruct this passage, including the precise source of the locally Lipschitz angular factor and the compatibility with the one-sided trace convention.

I do not identify a counterexample from the written argument. I do regard this as a load-bearing continuum point which finite definability checks cannot certify.

## 7. Exact barycentric representation

On one regular chamber set

\[
 \ell=b-a,
 \qquad
 \mathscr F(\theta,s)=a(\theta)+s\ell(\theta),
 \qquad 0<s<1.
\]

The measure

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon
 =c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)\,d\theta\,ds
\]

is exactly the paired source. Indeed the substitution

\[
 u=a+s\ell,
 \qquad du=\ell\,ds
\]

gives

\[
 c^\varepsilon\ell\,ds\,d\theta
 =c^\varepsilon\,du\,d\theta.
\]

Therefore the roof pushforward with the original Borel selector is the original trace density \(T_H^\varepsilon\). The segment length is not lost, and the minimum is taken before physical projection and before any norm.

This is the right positive representation. It does not replace the original collision probability or alter the guard, section, labels or target selector.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 8. The transverse Jacobian
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 8. The transverse Jacobian

Put

\[
 v(\theta,s)=\partial_\theta\mathscr F
 =(1-s)a'(\theta)+s b'(\theta).
\]

On \(v\ne0\), the field

\[
 V^\perp=v^{-1}\partial_\theta
\]

satisfies

\[
 \frac{d}{dh}\mathscr F(\Theta_h^\perp y)=1
\]

and preserves \(s\). In the coordinates

\[
 (t,s)=(\mathscr F,s)
\]

the paired measure is

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon
 =\varrho^\varepsilon(t,s)\,dt\,ds,
 \qquad
 \varrho^\varepsilon=\frac{c^\varepsilon\ell}{|v|}.
\]

The displayed ratio

\[
 J_h^\perp(y)
 =\frac{\varrho^\varepsilon(\Theta_h^\perp y)}
        {\varrho^\varepsilon(y)}
\]

is consistent with the **pullback** Jacobian convention used in module 245:

\[
 J_h^\perp(y)\,d\pi^
arepsilon(y)
\]

transforms to the paired measure at the translated roof. Under this convention the direction of the ratio is correct. The absolute value in \(|v|\) is essential and is correctly retained.

The manuscript should state explicitly that this is the pullback Jacobian, or write the precise integral covariance immediately beside its definition. Without that convention, readers often use the reciprocal Radon--Nikodym convention for a pushforward Jacobian. The subsequent proof makes the intended convention recoverable, but this should not remain implicit in a load-bearing theorem.

The transverse flow is a comparison between actual trajectories inside the same exact-event chamber. It is not the physical roof flow. This distinction is stated correctly.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 9. Multiplicity and physical summation
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 9. Multiplicity and physical summation

The new estimate must work after physical summation; a sheetwise modulus followed by an uncontrolled sum would not answer the previous report.

The manuscript relies on the inherited Borel bijection of actual maximal segments. Chamber interiors are counted once, compatible coordinate seams are continued, and the stopped flow is one-to-one on its graph. Since the positive covariance is applied before the uniform norm, the proof does not introduce the number of symbolic words, the number of chambers or a transverse-overlap factor.

This is the correct architecture. The principal specialist question is whether the one-to-one statement remains valid across every compatible continuation and whether every genuine loss of uniqueness or chamber regularity is indeed sent to the failure source. The proof says so and does not discard that failure source. I found no explicit double count in the formulas.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 10. The averaged complete paired source
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 10. The averaged complete paired source

Let \(\mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon\) be the complete paired source on

\[
 0<\ell<\Delta
\]

inside the original exact event, with no additional target selection.

The inherited trace comparison gives, schematically,

\[
 \mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon
 \le b^\varepsilon
 +C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
       \mathbf 1_{[-\Delta,\Delta]}*v^0.
\]

Applying the fixed-width averaging operator

\[
 A_rh(t)=\frac1{2r}\int_{t-r}^{t+r}h(u)\,du
\]

and using translation invariance yields

\[
 \|A_r(\mathbf1_{[-\Delta,\Delta]}*v^0)\|_\infty
 \le 2\Delta\|A_rv^0\|_\infty.
\]

Together with the inherited bounds for \(A_rb^\varepsilon\) and \(A_rv^0\), this gives

\[
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2
 \|A_r\mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon\|_\infty
 \le C\{\varepsilon^{1/16}+(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta\}.
\]

This derivation does not require a pointwise bound for \(v^0\). The factor \(2\Delta\) is harmless and can be absorbed in the universal constant. The constants are asserted independent of the previously fixed widths, exactly as required by the later schedule.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 11. The capped transverse clock
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 11. The capped transverse clock

The clock is

\[
 k_{r,\Delta}^\perp(y)
 =\frac1r\int_{-r}^{r}
   \mathbf1_{\{\Theta_h^\perp y\text{ exists}\}}
   \min\{1,J_h^\perp(y)\}\,dh.
\]

Its range is \([0,2]\), because the normalization is \(1/r\), not \(1/(2r)\). The admission threshold is chosen in \((0,1]\).

For an admitted starting point,

\[
 q_\perp\le k_{r,\Delta}^\perp.
\]

Multiplication by the target-fiber paired kernel and integration in \(h\) gives

\[
 q_\perp T_{H,\mathrm{adm}}^
arepsilon(t)
 \le \frac1r\int_{-r}^{r}
 \mathsf T_\Delta^
arepsilon(t+h)\,dh.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
 T_{H,\mathrm{adm}}^
arepsilon(t)
 \le \frac1{q_\perp r}
 \int_{t-r}^{t+r}\mathsf T_\Delta^
arepsilon(u)\,du.
\]

The proof uses

\[
 \min\{1,J_h^\perp\}\le J_h^\perp
\]

and the target-direction covariance on the one-to-one survivor graph. The starting selector is held at the original roof. After transport, the selector is dropped only for a positive upper bound by the complete short paired source; the exact displacement, occupation, collision count and section event are not enlarged.

The factor relating the right-hand side to \(A_r\mathsf T_\Delta^
arepsilon\) is \(2/q_\perp\). It is correctly absorbed into the constant in the stated height theorem.

Thus, at its stated scope, module 245 genuinely estimates the positive common trace itself on the admitted set.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 12. The relative two-ended certificate
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 12. The relative two-ended certificate

The certificate assumes on one angular side, at fixed relative position \(s\), that

\[
 |v|\ge\nu>0,
\]

and that

\[
 |\partial_	heta\log\ell|,
 \quad |\partial_	heta\log c^
arepsilon|,
 \quad |\partial_	heta\log|v||
 \le A.
\]

If

\[
 r\le \nu\min\{L_	heta,\log2/(3A)\},
\]

then the required roof displacement is reached before leaving the angular interval, and

\[
 \ell(\theta)\le 2^{1/3}\delta<2\delta,
 \qquad
 \frac{\varrho^
arepsilon(\theta,s)}
      {\varrho^
arepsilon(\theta_0,s)}
 \ge\frac12.
\]

One full one-sided interval of roof length \(r\) therefore contributes at least

\[
 \frac1r\cdot r\cdot\frac12=\frac12
\]

to the clock.

The calculation is correct and explains why a lower bound on the original residence \(\ell(\theta_0)\) is not intrinsically necessary. Parallel moving endpoint roofs provide a useful model of that cancellation.

The limitation is decisive. The certificate requires a positive transverse speed, sufficient one-sided angular reach and relative logarithmic control of three quantities. None of those conditions is proved uniformly on the full physical pairing family. In particular, when a backward-critical entrance has \(a'=0\), one has

\[
 v=s b'.
\]

The certificate may work for interior \(s\), but degenerates as \(s\downarrow0\). The potentially positive critical trace at that corner remains in the failure source.

A conditional certificate is not a deconcentration theorem for its complement.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 13. Schedule and exponent audit
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 13. Schedule and exponent audit

The inherited outer schedule is

\[
 \varepsilon(B)=A_0B^{-1/12},
 \qquad q_0^*=1/8,
 \qquad r_0=c\varepsilon^4,
 \qquad \delta=6q_0^*r_0.
\]

The new choices are

\[
 \Delta=2\delta,
 \qquad r_\perp=\delta,
 \qquad q_\perp=\varepsilon^{1/32}.
\]

Substitution into the admitted-height estimate gives

\[
 q_\perp^{-1}\varepsilon^{1/16}
 =\varepsilon^{1/32}
\]

and

\[
 q_\perp^{-1}(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta
 =O(\varepsilon^{95/32}).
\]

Since \(\varepsilon=B^{-1/12}\), the first term is

\[
 B^{-1/384}.
\]

The retained terms

\[
 B^{-1/192},
 \qquad \varepsilon^{257/64},
 \qquad \varepsilon^3
\]

all decay faster. I found no exponent error in the displayed schedule.

Every new threshold is fixed as a function of the outer reconstruction parameter before the collision limit. No new cutoff depends on the collision count.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 14. The remaining failure source
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 14. The remaining failure source

Define

\[
 \mathsf U_B
 =T_{\mathsf S,\mathrm{fail}}^{\varepsilon(B)}.
\]

The exact positive split is

\[
 T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon(B)}
 =T_{\mathsf S,\mathrm{adm}}^{\varepsilon(B)}+\mathsf U_B.
\]

The new theorem proves

\[
 \mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S,\mathrm{adm}}^{\varepsilon(B)})
 \le C\bigl(\varepsilon^{1/32}+
arepsilon^{95/32}\bigr)
\]

and hence

\[
 \mathcal E_M
 \le \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)+C_MB^{-1/384}.
\]

No bound is proved for \(\mathsf U_B\). It is not shown to have small total mass, small weak type, bounded overlap, a vanishing residence factor, or any positive power compatible with the outer schedule. Even a small mass estimate would not by itself imply the required essential-height decay.

The failure source can include the most singular configurations: stationary endpoint roofs, folds, short comparison lifetimes, critical corners and rapidly varying positive trace weights. These are precisely the configurations capable of producing a pointwise upper spike.

The theorem that the original pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\to0
\]

is useful and internally consistent with the inherited positive scalar decomposition. It also confirms that the principal theorem remains open.

## 16. What revision 102 does not establish

all_original_sections.original_text: ## 17. Required changes before another top-four review

\]

under a legal outer schedule, or replace this quantity by a strictly smaller remainder whose decay is proved. Renaming or repartitioning the positive failure source is not enough.

all_original_sections.original_text:

A successful theorem could take either of two forms:

1. prove that the relative two-ended certificate holds, with quantitative constants, on all physical pairs selected by the original source except a part already known to have vanishing ordered height; or
2. prove directly that failure of the certificate forces a geometric degeneracy whose physically summed positive trace has a vanishing essential-height bound.

The proof must address zero speed, short angular reach, folds and rapid relative variation rather than assigning them to an uncontrolled remainder.

all_original_sections.original_text:

A finite-mass, weak-convergence, fixed finite-\(p\), or averaged-roof estimate does not close the theorem. The result must imply essential-height decay with an explicit exponent compatible with

\[
 \varepsilon(B)\asymp B^{-1/12},
 \qquad \delta\asymp\varepsilon^4.
\]

all_original_sections.original_text:

 J_h^\perp(y)d\pi^
arepsilon(y)
 \mapsto d\pi^
arepsilon(\Theta_h^\perp y),

## 20. Final assessment
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 20. Final assessment

Revision 102 responds positively and mathematically to the revision-100 report. It no longer estimates only a trace difference. It represents the original positive paired minimum exactly, constructs a transverse paired measure, proves a physically summed capped-clock inequality, supplies an explicit local admission certificate and obtains a legal \(B^{-1/384}\) rate for the admitted source.

I found no decisive internal error in modules 244--246 at their stated scope. The new Jacobian and exponent bookkeeping are coherent, subject to the specialist checks listed above.

Nevertheless, the manuscript retains the complete nonadmitted positive source and proves no decay for it. The original pointwise theorem is explicitly equivalent to the vanishing of that source. The principal referee request, upper pointwise theorem, full exact-label raw local limit theorem and unrestricted downstream consequences therefore remain open.

**Final recommendation: reject in the present form at the requested four-journal benchmark.**

revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revision 102 is an actual theorem-bearing author revision. It repairs the submission-state defect identified in the revision-101 report: both named author branches point to the same new author commit, the active manuscript directory exists, and the packet contains a new article, three new proof modules, a source manifest, an itemized response and a dedicated exact-SHA workflow.

The mathematical response is also genuine. Revision 100 had reduced the unresolved upper pointwise problem to the positive same-segment minimum of two physical endpoint traces. That quantity could remain large even when the outgoing-minus-incoming trace difference and the associated volume source were small. Revision 102 now acts on this **positive minimum itself**. It introduces the barycentric representation

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon
 =c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)\,d\theta\,ds,
 \qquad
 \mathscr F(\theta,s)=a(\theta)+s\ell(\theta),
\]

where

\[
 c^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\min\{f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta),f^\varepsilon(b-,\theta)\}.
\]

It then uses the transverse field

\[
 V^\perp=(\partial_\theta\mathscr F)^{-1}\partial_\theta
\]

on regular pairing chambers, computes the paired-measure Jacobian, and proves a finite-count capped-clock comparison for the positive admitted source after physical sheets have been summed. Under the inherited schedule, the admitted source has normalized essential height

\[
 O(B^{-1/384}).
\]

This is substantive progress. It is not merely a renamed trace-difference estimate, a volume collar, a signed Jordan component or an averaged version of the target.

I audited the new modules

- `core/244_barycentric_positive_trace_coarea.tex`;
- `core/245_transverse_clock_and_pointwise_trace_height.tex`;
- `core/246_transverse_certificates_and_scalar_schedule.tex`;

and their dependence on the focused inputs, the revision-100 report, the response, the proof ledger, the source manifest and the principal pointwise target. Within the stated admitted scope, I found no decisive sign error, missing factor of the segment length, reversed transverse speed, exponent error, illegal collision-dependent cutoff, or hidden word-count factor.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the new argument. The scalar theorem is now

\[
 \mathcal E_M
 \le \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)+C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

where \(\mathsf U_B\) is the complete positive paired source on which the transverse clock fails. The manuscript explicitly retains in \(\mathsf U_B\):

- zero transverse speed;
- insufficient one-sided transverse reach;
- actual loss of pairing regularity;
- nonregular pairing strata carrying positive paired mass;
- uncontrolled logarithmic variation of the residence, paired weight or speed;
- folds of the endpoint roof maps; and
- positive backward-critical traces which are not admitted near the critical corner.

No estimate proves

\[
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\longrightarrow0.
\]

Indeed the manuscript proves that, along the unchanged outer schedule, the original pointwise theorem is equivalent to this limit. Thus the unresolved failure source is not a secondary remainder after the principal theorem. It is exactly the remaining upper obstruction.

The conditional certificate in module 246 is useful, but it is not verified uniformly on the complete physical pairing family. It gives a sufficient local criterion, not a theorem that the complement of the criterion has small mass or small essential height. The failure source could still carry the entire upper spike allowed by the previous reduction.

Consequently revision 102 does not prove the upper pointwise half, the unrestricted exact-label raw local limit theorem, or the unrestricted point-conditioned consequences organized by that theorem. At the requested benchmark, replacing one explicit positive source by a smaller explicit positive source is valuable progress but not closure of the governing result.

## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

There is no new revision-103 mathematical manuscript to review.

The only visible branch carrying the revision-103 label resolves to

`37faf38478a5b561c3aa4a1faf63da378caf8189`,

whose commit message is

`Review A2-DYN v102 at the top-four mathematics benchmark`.

Relative to the actual revision-102 author commit

`0cc27da5fbfb480e9a8fdbe7631ed3f869c99cd9`,

that head is one commit ahead and adds exactly one file:

`reviews/a2-dyn-v102-external-top4-review-2026-10-13/REFEREE_REPORT.md`.

It does not add a directory `papers/A2-DYN-v103-referee-response`, a revision-103 source manifest, a revision-103 qualification workflow, a revision-103 referee-copy author branch, or any theorem-bearing source. There is also no GitHub Actions run for the visible revision-103 branch. The revision-103 label is therefore a branch alias for an external-review commit, not a mathematical revision.

The latest actual author manuscript remains revision 102 at

`0cc27da5fbfb480e9a8fdbe7631ed3f869c99cd9`.

That manuscript has already received a full 732-line top-four referee report. The report found substantial progress in the positive same-segment trace problem but identified one exact unresolved positive source. I have repeated a focused supplementary audit of the submission identity, the central scalar reduction, the final schedule, and the qualification evidence which was incomplete at the freeze of the existing report.

The mathematical assessment does not change. Revision 102 proves an essential-height estimate for the **admitted** positive paired trace, with rate

\[
O(B^{-1/384}),
\]

but leaves the complete positive transverse-failure source

\[
\mathsf U_B
\]

uncontrolled. Its final scalar theorem is

\[
\mathcal E_M
\le \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)+C_MB^{-1/384}.
\]

No theorem proves

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\longrightarrow0.
\]

The manuscript further proves that, along the unchanged outer schedule, the original pointwise theorem is equivalent to this missing limit. The unresolved source is therefore the remaining upper obstruction itself, not a harmless remainder after the main theorem.

Successful completion of both exact-SHA qualification runs strengthens the source and build record. It does not supply the missing positive deconcentration theorem and does not alter the top-four recommendation.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 3. Updated qualification evidence
## 4. Scope of this supplementary audit
## 5. The positive barycentric source
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 5. The positive barycentric source

Revision 102 acts on the positive common boundary trace itself, rather than only on a signed trace difference. On a regular pairing chamber it writes

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon
 =c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)\,d\theta\,ds,
 \qquad
 \mathscr F(\theta,s)=a(\theta)+s\ell(\theta),
\]

where

\[
 c^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\min\{f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta),f^\varepsilon(b-,\theta)\}.
\]

This representation is materially stronger than a volume-collar estimate. It retains the positive minimum of the two endpoint traces and parametrizes the entire same-segment paired source by the relative position \(s\in[0,1]\).

On a regular chamber the transverse vector field is

\[
 V^\perp=(\partial_\theta\mathscr F)^{-1}\partial_\theta.
\]

If

\[
 v(\theta,s)=\partial_\theta\mathscr F(	heta,s)
\]

is nonzero, the paired measure in target-roof coordinates has density proportional to

\[
 \frac{c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)}{|v(\theta,s)|}.
\]

Within the stated regular scope, the factor of \(\ell\), the reciprocal transverse speed and the orientation of the stopped flow are consistent with the change of variables. I found no missing residence factor in this calculation.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 6. What the transverse clock proves
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 6. What the transverse clock proves

The capped transverse clock averages the positive paired source over a bounded roof interval while preserving relative endpoint position. After physical sheets are summed, the manuscript obtains multiplicity one in the target direction and avoids an unweighted symbolic-word count.

For the admitted source it proves an estimate of the schematic form

\[
 \mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S,\mathrm{adm}}^\varepsilon)
 \le C\left(q_\perp^{-1}\varepsilon^{1/16}
 +q_\perp^{-1}(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta\right)
\]

plus inherited faster-decaying terms.

This is genuinely a pointwise essential-height estimate for the positive admitted trace, not merely a mass estimate, a signed cancellation, a finite-\(p\) norm or an averaged-roof statement.

The theorem remains conditional on admission. The clock does not show that all physical paired mass is admitted, and it does not estimate the positive complement.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 7. The two-ended certificate
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 7. The two-ended certificate

The local certificate assumes on one angular side, at fixed relative position \(s\), that

\[
 |v|\ge\nu>0
\]

and that the logarithmic derivatives of the residence, the positive paired weight and the transverse speed are bounded by a constant \(A\). If the required transverse roof displacement is smaller than both the available angular reach and the logarithmic-control scale, then the clock accumulates a definite amount before leaving the regular side.

This explains an important feature: no lower bound on the original residence \(\ell(\theta_0)\) is intrinsically needed, because the residence factor in the paired density cancels against the time needed to traverse the target roof interval.

The certificate is a useful sufficient criterion. It is not a theorem that the criterion holds uniformly on the complete physical pairing family, and it does not show that failure of the criterion has small essential height.

In particular, at a backward-critical entrance one can have

\[
 v=s b'.
\]

The transverse speed may therefore vanish as \(s\downarrow0\). The corresponding positive critical trace is not removed and remains part of the failure source.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 8. Schedule and exponent check
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 8. Schedule and exponent check

The inherited outer schedule is

\[
 \varepsilon(B)=A_0B^{-1/12},
 \qquad q_0^*=1/8,
 \qquad r_0=c\varepsilon^4,
 \qquad \delta=6q_0^*r_0.
\]

Revision 102 takes

\[
 \Delta=2\delta,
 \qquad r_\perp=\delta,
 \qquad q_\perp=\varepsilon^{1/32}.
\]

Then

\[
 q_\perp^{-1}\varepsilon^{1/16}
 =\varepsilon^{1/32}
 =O(B^{-1/384}),
\]

while

\[
 q_\perp^{-1}(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta
 =O(\varepsilon^{95/32})
\]

and the inherited terms decay faster. Every threshold is fixed from the outer reconstruction parameter before the collision limit. I found no exponent or order-of-limits error in this scalar schedule.

The rate applies only to the admitted positive source.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 9. The unresolved positive failure source
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 9. The unresolved positive failure source

The complete positive trace is split exactly as

\[
 T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon(B)}
 =T_{\mathsf S,\mathrm{adm}}^{\varepsilon(B)}+\mathsf U_B.
\]

The unresolved source \(\mathsf U_B\) can contain:

- zero transverse speed;
- insufficient one-sided angular reach;
- loss of pairing regularity;
- nonregular strata carrying positive paired mass;
- folds of endpoint roof maps;
- rapid logarithmic variation of residence, weight or speed;
- short comparison lifetimes; and
- positive backward-critical traces near the critical corner.

No estimate proves that this source has small total mass, weak type, bounded overlap, vanishing residence factor or essential height. Even a small total-mass statement would not by itself close the pointwise upper theorem.

The exact final reduction is

\[
 \mathcal E_M
 \le \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)+C_MB^{-1/384}.
\]

The manuscript identifies the original upper pointwise assertion with

\[
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\to0.
\]

This is a useful sharpening of the obstruction. It is not its solution.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 11.2. Control the entire failure source
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 11.2. Control the entire failure source

The next mathematical revision must prove

\[
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\longrightarrow0
\]

under a legal outer schedule, or replace \(\mathsf U_B\) by a strictly smaller positive remainder whose decay is actually proved.

Renaming, repartitioning or adding another conditional admission layer is not enough.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 11.3. Prove uniform admission or quantitative failure decay
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 11.3. Prove uniform admission or quantitative failure decay

A successful route could either:

1. prove that the relative two-ended certificate holds quantitatively on all physical pairs selected by the original source except a part already known to have vanishing ordered height; or
2. prove that failure of the certificate forces a geometric degeneracy whose physically summed positive trace has a schedule-compatible essential-height bound.

The proof must address zero speed, short angular reach, folds and rapid relative variation rather than assigning them to an uncontrolled positive remainder.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 11.4. Treat backward-critical corners explicitly
### 11.5. Work after physical summation
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 11.5. Work after physical summation

Any sheetwise estimate must be formulated after physical summation or accompanied by a collision-uniform bounded-overlap or capacity theorem. An unweighted symbolic-word count or chamber count cannot appear in the final bound.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 11.6. Retain the pointwise norm
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 11.6. Retain the pointwise norm

A mass estimate, weak convergence, fixed finite-\(p\) control or averaged-roof statement does not close the theorem. The conclusion must imply essential-height decay with a rate compatible with

\[
 \varepsilon(B)\asymp B^{-1/12},
 \qquad \delta\asymp\varepsilon^4.
\]

### 11.8. Preserve source and review identity
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 11.8. Preserve source and review identity

Future revision branches should begin from the latest report history if desired, but their final heads must be new author commits. Historical reports should remain immutable. New review branches should add reports only after freezing the author SHA.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 12. Exposition and editorial strategy
## 13. Significance and venue assessment
## 14. Final assessment
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 14. Final assessment

The visible revision-103 branch is not a new manuscript. It is an alias for the existing revision-102 review commit.

The latest actual mathematical source is revision 102. Its dedicated response and referee-copy workflows have now completed successfully, strengthening the provenance and build evidence. Its admitted transverse-clock estimate is a genuine advance, and I found no new decisive inconsistency in the focused chain.

The complete positive transverse-failure source remains uncontrolled. Therefore the upper pointwise theorem, the unrestricted exact-label raw local limit theorem and their unrestricted downstream consequences remain unproved.

**Final recommendation: reject in the present form at the requested four-journal benchmark.**

A new substantive review should begin only after a genuine author SHA is landed and either the complete positive failure source is controlled or the governing theorem is replaced by a completed result of comparable independent significance.

Revision 103 changes the comparison coordinates on the same positive paired measure, constructs two endpoint-distance clocks, identifies the regular critical incoming trace, separates exact zero-speed flat pulses, and recovers a positive portion of the preceding three-clock failure source. Revision 104 then introduces a different comparison which does not divide by an endpoint velocity at all. It compares angular intervals by positive segment inclusion and integrated trace mass, proves a finite-count pointwise inequality, and applies it to stationary-critical arms. On those arms it also pays the entire outgoing-trace shortage by the inherited uncut optical variation, so no lower bound on the outgoing trace fraction is required.

I audited the newly landed modules

- `core/247_endpoint_distance_coarea_and_critical_traces.tex`;
- `core/248_gap_clock_pointwise_recovery.tex`;
- `core/249_expanding_endpoint_certificate.tex`;
- `core/250_positive_angular_interval_comparison.tex`;
- `core/251_stationary_critical_arm_recovery.tex`;
- `core/252_positive_deficit_and_original_endpoint.tex`;

as well as the focused article, the response, the proof ledger, the source manifest, the qualification record, and the revision-102 substantive report which posed the positive-source obstruction.

Within the stated scopes I found no decisive sign error, missing segment-length factor, reversed Jacobian, incorrect exponent arithmetic, illegal exchange of the collision limit with the outer bandwidth, hidden differentiation of the Borel selector, or unaccounted word-count factor. The positive angular-interval comparison in module 250 is particularly clean: it uses only a product-a.e. interval inclusion, an integrated source/comparison mass balance, and a bounded physical overlap. The deficit

\[
  (C_j-\kappa D_j)_+
\]

is retained as an actual positive shortage, not assigned zero or absorbed into a signed cancellation. In module 251 the identity

\[
  D_j=P_j-E_j,
  \qquad
  E_j=\int_{J_j}[f_-^\varepsilon-f_+^\varepsilon]_+\,d\theta,
\]

and the estimate \(C_j\le \kappa P_j\) give the correct algebraic bound

\[
  (C_j-\kappa D_j)_+\le \kappa E_j.
\]

Subject to the inherited weighted-variation input and multiplicity-one physical summation, the subsequent payment of \(E_j\) by the original uncut volume is internally coherent.

The new estimates are therefore meaningful. In the strongest uniform arm class they give essential height

\[
  O(B^{-1/192}),
\]

and under the allowed outer balance budget they give

\[
  O(B^{-1/384}).
\]

They also cover positive-measure configurations on which all three preceding clocks can be small.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the new scalar theorem. After the entire certified stationary-critical arm source and its outgoing-trace shortage have been removed, the article obtains

\[
  \mathcal E_M
  \le
  \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm outside})
  +C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

and proves that the original exact-label pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
  \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm outside})\longrightarrow0.
\]

No theorem establishes this limit. The outside source still includes, among other possibilities,

- flat endpoint pulses on isolated chambers with no admissible comparison interval;
- loss of physical continuation before the comparison levels are reached;
- singular critical extensions not covered by the regular critical trace formula;
- simultaneous or higher-order endpoint stationarity without a schedule-compatible level-width budget;
- families for which the comparison intervals do not have a uniform physical overlap bound;
- nonstationary positive pairs not covered by the stationary-arm geometry; and
- any remaining trace shortage outside the critical incoming normalization.

The source manifest and publication status correctly keep complete physical coverage, full positive-deficit decay, all-three-clock failure decay, flat-pulse decay, the full raw-return local limit theorem, and closure of the primary referee request false.

Thus the manuscript has again reduced the governing positive obstruction to a smaller and better-structured positive obstruction, but it has not proved that the final obstruction vanishes. Since the paper itself proves equivalence between the organizing pointwise theorem and that missing limit, this is not an optional refinement after the main result. It is the unresolved upper pointwise half of the main result.

At the requested benchmark, a technically serious partial deconcentration theorem does not substitute for the exact-label raw pointwise local limit theorem around which the article is organized. A positive recommendation would require either closure of the complete outside source or a separate theorem of independent breadth and significance whose statement does not depend on the unfinished endpoint. Revision 104 supplies neither yet.

## 4. Scope of this review
## 5. The inherited positive obstruction
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 5. The inherited positive obstruction

Revision 102 had reached the positive paired source

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon
 =c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)\,d\theta\,ds,
 \qquad
 c^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\min\{f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta),f^\varepsilon(b-,\theta)\},
\]

with roof map

\[
 \mathscr F(\theta,s)=a(	heta)+s\ell(	heta),
 \qquad \ell=b-a.
\]

The pointwise difficulty is the positive minimum itself. Both endpoint traces can be large and close, so a small signed trace difference does not control this minimum. Revision 102 gave a pointwise height estimate only on the source admitted by a relative transverse clock. Its scalar theorem left the positive clock-failure source as the exact upper obstruction.

Revision 103 and revision 104 attack that correct object. Neither replaces it by a signed current, an average on the left, a volume collar, a different event, or a finite norm weaker than the target essential height.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 6. Revision 103: endpoint-distance coordinates
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 6. Revision 103: endpoint-distance coordinates

Module 247 replaces the barycentric relative coordinate by the roof distances

\[
 x_-=u-a(	heta),
 \qquad
 x_+=b(	heta)-u.
\]

Since \(x_-=s\ell\) and \(x_+=(1-s)\ell\), the factor \(\ell\) in the barycentric measure is exactly the coordinate Jacobian, and in either coordinate

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon=c^\varepsilon(	heta)\,d	heta\,dx_\pm.
\]

This is an exact change of variables on the same positive measure.

At fixed \(x_\pm\), the roof derivative is \(e_\pm'\), so the unit-roof-speed fields have densities

\[
 \rho_\pm^\varepsilon=
rac{c^\varepsilon}{|e_\pm'|}.
\]

The pullback Jacobian

\[
 J_h^\pm(y)
 =\frac{\rho_\pm^\varepsilon(\Theta_h^\pm y)}
        {\rho_\pm^\varepsilon(y)}
\]

has the correct orientation for the displayed covariance identity. The absolute speed is retained. I found no missing \(\ell\)-factor or reciprocal error in this coordinate change.

The finite-count pointwise comparison in module 248 disjointizes the source by the first successful endpoint-distance clock. Each admitted part is transported through the exact covariance and bounded by the complete short paired target. The factor two counts the two explicitly chosen comparison directions, not the number of words or chambers. Since the source selector remains at the starting roof and the target comparison is positive, no selector derivative or signed cancellation is needed.

Under the stated schedule the recovered part has height \(O(B^{-1/384})\). The exact positive split

\[
 \mathsf U_B
 =\mathsf V_B+\mathsf U_B^{\rm rem}
\]

is valid at finite count, with \(0\le \mathsf U_B^{\rm rem}\le \mathsf U_B\).

These arguments are coherent within their admitted domain.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 7. Critical trace and exact zero speed
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 7. Critical trace and exact zero speed

Module 247 computes the regular nongrazing backward-critical incoming trace as

\[
 f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta)
 =\frac{\omega(q_*)W^\varepsilon(q_*)}
 {4\pi c_*\,e_\perp(\theta)^{\mathsf T}K_*e_\perp(\theta)}.
\]

This formula correctly permits a positive trace. It does not infer that the positive minimum with the outgoing trace has controlled relative variation. That distinction was essential in the previous reports and is preserved.

The exact zero-speed lemma is also appropriately limited. If at least one endpoint derivative is nonzero, the relative speed vanishes at at most one \(s\)-value and is paired-measure null. When both endpoint derivatives vanish on a definable interval, the endpoint roofs are constant there and the source is an explicit positive rectangular pulse. The article does not declare those pulses negligible.

The load-bearing issues for a specialist are the one-sided critical trace convention, the regularity of the physical extension, and the definable classification of the common derivative-zero set. I found no contradiction in the written argument, but these continuum points are not certified by the finite fixtures.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 8. The expanding-endpoint certificate
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 8. The expanding-endpoint certificate

Module 249 proves a sufficient certificate under

\[
 |\dot e|\ge\nu,
 \qquad
 0\le\dot\ell\le K|\dot e|,
 \qquad
 |(\log c^\varepsilon)^{\boldsymbol\cdot}|\le A,
 \qquad
 |(\log|\dot e|)^{\boldsymbol\cdot}|\le A,
\]

and the corresponding one-sided reach and scale conditions.

Keeping the distance to the selected endpoint fixed is the correct construction. Because the residence is nondecreasing, every initial relative position remains inside the segment, including approach to either endpoint. The density ratio then gives a clock bounded below without a logarithmic derivative of the residence. The opposite-slope corollary and the two elementary models correctly demonstrate why the endpoint-distance clocks can recover positive source missed by the relative clock.

The theorem remains a certificate. It does not prove that every physical pair has the speed, trace-variation and reach properties. Flat pulses, simultaneous stationarity, short reach and rapid trace variation remain outside. Revision 104 is designed to remove the endpoint-speed requirement on an important stationary-critical family.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 9. Revision 104: positive angular-interval comparison
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 9. Revision 104: positive angular-interval comparison

Module 250 is the conceptual center of revision 104. It assumes source angular sets \(I_j\), comparison sets \(J_j\), and one-sided interval inclusion. For the positive masses

\[
 C_j=\int_{I_j}c\,d\theta,
 \qquad
 D_j=\int_{J_j}c\,d\theta,
\]

it sets

\[
 \alpha_j=\min\{1,\kappa D_j/C_j\}
\]

when \(C_j>0\).

If the selected source at a roof \(t\) is positive, the product-a.e. inclusion implies that almost every comparison angle contains the appropriate one-sided interval of roofs of length \(r\). Hence

\[
 rD_j
 \le
 \int_{t+\tau_j(0,r)}T_{J_j}(u)\,du,
 \qquad
 \alpha_jT_{H,j}(t)
 \le \alpha_jC_j
 \le\kappa D_j.
\]

Summing and using the physical overlap bound gives

\[
 \sum_j\alpha_jT_{H,j}(t)
 \le
 \frac{N\kappa}{r}
 \int_{t-r}^{t+r}\mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon(u)\,du.
\]

The quantifiers are sound: positivity of the selected integral gives a source set of positive angular measure, and Fubini converts the product-a.e. inclusion into the needed statement for almost every comparison angle. The proof does not require a pointwise map from each source trajectory to a comparison trajectory.

The exact positive remainder satisfies

\[
 (1-\alpha_j)C_j=(C_j-\kappa D_j)_+.
\]

This is the correct deficit. The theorem neither differentiates the positive minimum nor divides by any endpoint or relative speed. It therefore genuinely reaches stationary endpoint geometries missed by the preceding clocks.

The theorem is conditional on the interval inclusion, mass balance and physical overlap. Its strength on the Lorentz family depends entirely on verifying those conditions on a sufficiently complete family.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 10. Stationary-critical arm balance
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 10. Stationary-critical arm balance

On a regular critical arm the incoming roof is constant and

\[
 f_-^\varepsilon(x)=\frac{N_*}{Q_*(x)},
 \qquad
 \lambda_\circ\le Q_*(x)\le\Lambda_\circ.
\]

The outgoing roof is written

\[
 b(x)=a_*+d+\psi(x),
 \qquad 0\le d\le\delta/2,
\]

with three actual reached levels. The source and comparison intervals are

\[
 I=(0,x_1),
 \qquad
 J=(x_2,x_3),
\]

where \(\psi(x_1)=\delta/2\), \(\psi(x_2)=2\delta\), and \(\psi(x_3)=3\delta\).

Writing

\[
 w=\min\{1,f_+^\varepsilon/f_-^\varepsilon\},
 \qquad
 \mu_J=|J|^{-1}\int_Jw,
\]

the estimate

\[
 \frac{\int_Ic^\varepsilon}
      {\int_Jc^\varepsilon}
 \le
 \frac{\Lambda_\circ}{\lambda_\circ\mu_J}
 \frac{x_1}{x_3-x_2}
\]

is correct. Under the elasticity bound

\[
 \frac{x\psi'(x)}{\psi(x)}\le K,
\]

integration of \(\psi'/\psi\) gives

\[
 x_3-x_2
 \ge x_1\frac{\log(3/2)}{K},
\]

and hence the displayed mass balance. No lower bound on \(\psi'\) is needed.

The interval inclusion is also correct: source lengths are at most \(\delta\), comparison lengths are below \(4\delta\), and the outgoing endpoint advances by more than \(\delta\). Disjoint physical arms give overlap one on the pairing-sheet space.

This proves a genuine pointwise height theorem for the certified stationary-critical arm source, including every relative position.

The theorem does not prove that every stationary-critical arm reaches the three levels before a true boundary, has a schedule-compatible level-width ratio, or belongs to a family with a uniform finite-order budget. Finite-count definability alone gives no uniform bound on the order, neighborhood or reach. The author states these limitations correctly.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 11. Paying the outgoing-trace shortage
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 11. Paying the outgoing-trace shortage

The strongest new step is Theorem `thm:v104-paid-arms`, which removes the lower bound on the average outgoing trace fraction.

For one comparison interval it defines

\[
 P_j=\int_{J_j}f_-^\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 E_j=\int_{J_j}[f_-^\varepsilon-f_+^\varepsilon]_+,
 \qquad
 D_j=P_j-E_j.
\]

The critical incoming normalization and geometric width ratio imply \(C_j\le\kappa P_j\), so

\[
 (C_j-\kappa D_j)_+
 \le\kappa E_j.
\]

This algebra is valid even if \(D_j=0\).

The inherited weighted variation bound is then used in the form

\[
 [f_-^\varepsilon(x)-f_+^\varepsilon(x)]_+
 \le
 C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
 \int_{a_j}^{b(x)}
       A(u,x)I_m(u,x)/z(u,x)\,du.
\]

Because the incoming roof is common on the arm, every comparison segment contributing to a source roof \(t\) lies in the common window

\[
 (t-\delta,t+4\delta).
\]

After summing disjoint comparison intervals on the original physical sheet space, the Borel segment identity charges the complete variation to the same uncut source \(v^0\) with multiplicity one. Only after that positive physical sum is formed does the proof apply the fixed-width averaged bound on \(v^0\).

This is the correct order. The argument does not assume a pointwise bound on \(v^0\), and it does not replace the original variation by an averaged trace difference on the left.

The step is nevertheless highly load-bearing. An independent specialist should verify line by line:

1. that the inherited derivative estimate applies to the same one-sided endpoint traces and guard used here;
2. that compact-interior integration passes to both endpoint traces without an unrecorded boundary measure;
3. that the comparison intervals are genuinely disjoint on the incident-component pairing-sheet space;
4. that no physical segment is counted twice when several arms meet a geometrical boundary point;
5. that the common incoming roof is preserved throughout the family being summed;
6. that the window \((t-\delta,t+4\delta)\) contains every paid segment with the stated endpoint conventions; and
7. that the inherited uncut volume estimate is uniform in the same labels and outer parameters.

I found no fatal inconsistency in the written proof, but the finite diagnostics do not establish these continuum and multiplicity assertions.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 12. The exact residual scalar decomposition
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 12. The exact residual scalar decomposition

Module 252 applies the comparison to the original selector \(H_B\) which already includes the short-source condition and failure of all three preceding clocks. It writes

\[
 \mathsf U_B^{\rm rem}
 =\mathsf V_B^{\rm int}+\mathsf R_B^{\rm int}
\]

at finite count, with both terms positive. The recovered part consists of the fractions \(\alpha_j\) on the chosen intervals. The remainder contains

- the entire source outside the chosen \(I_j\); and
- the explicit comparison deficits on the chosen \(I_j\).

If \(N_B\kappa_B\le C\varepsilon(B)^{-1/32}\), the recovered height is \(O(B^{-1/384})\); if \(N_B\kappa_B\) is bounded, it improves to \(O(B^{-1/192})\). The exponent arithmetic is correct for

\[
 \varepsilon(B)=A_0B^{-1/12},
 \qquad
 \delta=O(\varepsilon^4).
\]

On the paid stationary-critical arms the entire comparison deficit is bounded by

\[
 C\kappa_B(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\delta
 =O(\varepsilon^{95/32})
\]

under the allowed budget. Therefore the whole source on those arms, not only a trace-balanced fraction, is removed from the scalar obstruction.

What remains is exactly

\[
 \mathsf U_B^{\rm outside}
 =T_{H_B\mathbf 1_{(\cup I_j)^c}}^{\varepsilon(B)}.
\]

The final theorem is

\[
 \mathcal E_M
 \le
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm outside})
 +C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

with equivalence between the original pointwise theorem and the vanishing of this outside height.

This is a precise and honest endpoint. It is also an explicit statement that the principal theorem is not yet proved.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 13. The unresolved physical classes
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 13. The unresolved physical classes

The article identifies several mechanisms which can remain in the outside source.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 13.1. Flat endpoint pulses
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 13.1. Flat endpoint pulses

If both endpoint roofs are constant on a positive angular interval, the source is a positive rectangular roof pulse. Such a chamber may have no comparison interval satisfying the required one-sided inclusion. Revision 104 does not bound the total height of these pulses.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 13.2. Insufficient physical reach
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 13.2. Insufficient physical reach

The arm theorem requires that the actual physical continuation reaches the outgoing levels \(\delta/2\), \(2\delta\), and \(3\delta\) before a true endpoint, section change, singularity or loss of pairing. Algebraic continuation of the endpoint profile is not enough. No complete reach theorem is given.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 13.3. Singular critical extensions
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 13.3. Singular critical extensions

The critical incoming trace formula applies to a regular nongrazing stationary extension. Coincident singular extensions remain in the original source. They are not shown null or small in the target height norm.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 13.4. Unbounded order or width ratio
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 13.4. Unbounded order or width ratio

A finite-order asymptotic \(\psi(x)\sim\beta x^k\) gives a local elasticity bound, but the article does not prove a uniform order \(k\), a uniform asymptotic neighborhood or a schedule-compatible outer budget for every physical arm.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 13.5. General nonstationary pairs
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 13.5. General nonstationary pairs

The positive angular-interval theorem is abstract enough to handle other families, but no theorem constructs comparison pairs with controlled overlap and mass balance for the complete nonstationary remainder.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 13.6. General trace deficits
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 13.6. General trace deficits

The uncut-volume payment uses the stationary critical incoming normalization. Comparison families without that common normalization can still leave a positive deficit in \(\mathsf R_B^{\rm int}\).

Any one of these classes could, in principle, carry the remaining upper spike. The manuscript gives no global classification theorem proving otherwise.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 14. Why the missing limit is decisive
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 14. Why the missing limit is decisive

The full exact-label raw pointwise theorem is not merely one downstream corollary among many. It is the organizing statement of the article. The manuscript retains the original event, labels, guard, arithmetic zero classes and scalar-first order of proof. It also proves necessity: if the scalar pointwise conclusion holds, then the remaining positive source height must vanish.

Therefore the final outside-source estimate cannot be postponed as a technical improvement while the main theorem is declared complete. The article's own logic identifies it as the last upper obstruction.

Until that obstruction is closed, the paper cannot promote unrestricted point-conditioned kernels, denominators, same-roof ratios, likelihood laws or other downstream conclusions which require the full pointwise theorem. The author packet correctly refrains from doing so.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 15. Significance and architecture at the requested benchmark
## 16. Required changes before another top-four review
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 16. Required changes before another top-four review

A genuinely decisive revision should address the following items.

1. **Classify the complete outside source.** Give a theorem decomposing every remaining physical pairing sheet into finitely or countably many comparison classes with schedule-compatible overlap and mass balance, plus a residual class whose target height is proved small.

2. **Control flat endpoint pulses.** Prove their total essential height vanishes, compare them by a new positive mechanism, or establish a physical theorem excluding them except on a target-null set. Merely displaying the pulse is not enough.

3. **Prove physical reach.** Establish that every relevant stationary-critical arm reaches the required comparison levels before a true boundary, or quantify and control the source lost by failure of reach.

4. **Handle singular critical extensions.** Either extend the trace/interval argument to them or prove their complete positive source has negligible height in the original norm.

5. **Uniformize the level-width budget.** Show that the physical orders, elasticity constants and comparison widths satisfy the \(B\)-dependent budget on the complete family. Fixed-count definability does not supply this uniformity.

6. **Extend the paid-deficit mechanism.** For comparison families without the stationary incoming normalization, prove an analogous payment or a direct positive mass balance.

7. **Prove the final limit.** Establish

   \[
   \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm outside})\to0
   \]

   for every fixed \(M\), and then derive the exact-label pointwise theorem without changing the event, topology or order of limits.

8. **Obtain an independent specialist audit.** The physical sheet construction, critical trace, one-sided endpoint passage, uncut variation payment, multiplicity-one summation and inherited pressure/coarea inputs require expert verification independent of the author-side finite diagnostics.

9. **Keep downstream promotion conditional until scalar closure.** Denominators and unrestricted conditioned laws must follow only after the complete pointwise theorem is established.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 17. Technical and presentation comments
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 17. Technical and presentation comments

1. The introduction should state explicitly that the latest submission-state report did not review the subsequently landed revision-103 mathematics. The present source history is correct in Git, but a reader could otherwise mistake the v103 packet for an independently reviewed baseline.

2. The focused `main.tex` repeats the definitions of \(q,F,g,z,I_m\) verbatim in the inherited-source section. One copy should be removed.

3. The proof of Theorem `thm:v104-block` should spell out the Fubini quantifier in one sentence: from a positive selected source set and a product-null exceptional set, almost every comparison angle satisfies the inclusion for almost every selected source angle. The current proof is correct but terse at this point.

4. The statement of the stationary-arm theorem should distinguish clearly between disjoint source intervals and disjoint entire physical arms. The overlap-one conclusion uses disjointness of the comparison intervals on the incident-component sheet space, not merely disjointness of the source \(I_j\).

5. The paid-deficit theorem should cite the exact inherited theorem and endpoint convention supplying the weighted derivative bound, rather than only the focused input label. This is the most load-bearing imported estimate in revision 104.

6. A table should list, for every physical failure class, whether it is controlled by the relative clock, an endpoint-distance clock, the positive interval comparison, the uncut-volume deficit payment, or no current theorem. This would make the final outside source auditable.

7. The manuscript should keep the two rates separate throughout: \(O(B^{-1/192})\) requires a bounded balance cost, while \(O(B^{-1/384})\) permits the specified growing budget. Neither rate applies to the uncovered source.

8. Model interval calculations should remain labeled as model checks. They verify the comparison mechanism but do not establish realized Lorentz geometry or complete physical coverage.

9. The remote exact-SHA successes should be recorded in the final static source metadata. The manifest was written before publication and correctly says that remote publication was not yet observed; a later source revision may update the evidentiary record without changing the mathematical claims.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 18. Final assessment
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 18. Final assessment

Revisions 103 and 104 are substantive advances. They act on the correct positive paired source, introduce comparison mechanisms genuinely different from the original relative clock, cover certified critical-corner and opposite-slope geometries, eliminate the endpoint-speed requirement on stationary-critical arms, and pay the complete outgoing-trace shortage on those arms by the original uncut optical variation. I found no decisive mathematical error in the new six-module chain.

The source and build record is also strong: both author refs identify one commit and both exact-SHA workflows succeeded.

Nevertheless, the exact result proved is still a partial recovery theorem. The complete outside source is retained, its essential height is not shown to vanish, and the article proves that the original pointwise theorem is equivalent to precisely that missing limit. The full exact-label raw return local limit theorem and its unrestricted downstream consequences therefore remain unproved.

At the requested *Annals* / *Acta* / *Inventiones* / *JAMS* benchmark, the manuscript is not ready.

**Final recommendation: reject in the present form.**

## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revisions 103 and 104 contain genuine mathematical progress on the exact positive source left by revision 102. They are not branch aliases or bookkeeping-only packets. Revision 103 changes the comparison coordinates on the same positive paired measure, constructs two endpoint-distance clocks, identifies the regular critical incoming trace, separates exact zero-speed flat pulses, and recovers a positive portion of the preceding three-clock failure source. Revision 104 then introduces a different comparison which does not divide by an endpoint velocity at all. It compares angular intervals by positive segment inclusion and integrated trace mass, proves a finite-count pointwise inequality, and applies it to stationary-critical arms. On those arms it also pays the entire outgoing-trace shortage by the inherited uncut optical variation, so no lower bound on the outgoing trace fraction is required.

I audited the newly landed modules

- `core/247_endpoint_distance_coarea_and_critical_traces.tex`;
- `core/248_gap_clock_pointwise_recovery.tex`;
- `core/249_expanding_endpoint_certificate.tex`;
- `core/250_positive_angular_interval_comparison.tex`;
- `core/251_stationary_critical_arm_recovery.tex`;
- `core/252_positive_deficit_and_original_endpoint.tex`;

as well as the focused article, the response, the proof ledger, the source manifest, the qualification record, and the revision-102 substantive report which posed the positive-source obstruction.

Within the stated scopes I found no decisive sign error, missing segment-length factor, reversed Jacobian, incorrect exponent arithmetic, illegal exchange of the collision limit with the outer bandwidth, hidden differentiation of the Borel selector, or unaccounted word-count factor. The positive angular-interval comparison in module 250 is particularly clean: it uses only a product-a.e. interval inclusion, an integrated source/comparison mass balance, and a bounded physical overlap. The deficit

\[
  (C_j-\kappa D_j)_+
\]

is retained as an actual positive shortage, not assigned zero or absorbed into a signed cancellation. In module 251 the identity

\[
  D_j=P_j-E_j,
  \qquad
  E_j=\int_{J_j}[f_-^\varepsilon-f_+^\varepsilon]_+\,d\theta,
\]

and the estimate \(C_j\le \kappa P_j\) give the correct algebraic bound

\[
  (C_j-\kappa D_j)_+\le \kappa E_j.
\]

Subject to the inherited weighted-variation input and multiplicity-one physical summation, the subsequent payment of \(E_j\) by the original uncut volume is internally coherent.

The new estimates are therefore meaningful. In the strongest uniform arm class they give essential height

\[
  O(B^{-1/192}),
\]

and under the allowed outer balance budget they give

\[
  O(B^{-1/384}).
\]

They also cover positive-measure configurations on which all three preceding clocks can be small.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the new scalar theorem. After the entire certified stationary-critical arm source and its outgoing-trace shortage have been removed, the article obtains

\[
  \mathcal E_M
  \le
  \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm outside})
  +C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

and proves that the original exact-label pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
  \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm outside})\longrightarrow0.
\]

No theorem establishes this limit. The outside source still includes, among other possibilities,

- flat endpoint pulses on isolated chambers with no admissible comparison interval;
- loss of physical continuation before the comparison levels are reached;
- singular critical extensions not covered by the regular critical trace formula;
- simultaneous or higher-order endpoint stationarity without a schedule-compatible level-width budget;
- families for which the comparison intervals do not have a uniform physical overlap bound;
- nonstationary positive pairs not covered by the stationary-arm geometry; and
- any remaining trace shortage outside the critical incoming normalization.

The source manifest and publication status correctly keep complete physical coverage, full positive-deficit decay, all-three-clock failure decay, flat-pulse decay, the full raw-return local limit theorem, and closure of the primary referee request false.

Thus the manuscript has again reduced the governing positive obstruction to a smaller and better-structured positive obstruction, but it has not proved that the final obstruction vanishes. Since the paper itself proves equivalence between the organizing pointwise theorem and that missing limit, this is not an optional refinement after the main result. It is the unresolved upper pointwise half of the main result.

At the requested benchmark, a technically serious partial deconcentration theorem does not substitute for the exact-label raw pointwise local limit theorem around which the article is organized. A positive recommendation would require either closure of the complete outside source or a separate theorem of independent breadth and significance whose statement does not depend on the unfinished endpoint. Revision 104 supplies neither yet.

## 6. Revision 103: endpoint-distance coordinates
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 6. Revision 103: endpoint-distance coordinates

Module 247 replaces the barycentric relative coordinate by the roof distances

\[
 x_-=u-a(	heta),
 \qquad
 x_+=b(	heta)-u.
\]

Since \(x_-=s\ell\) and \(x_+=(1-s)\ell\), the factor \(\ell\) in the barycentric measure is exactly the coordinate Jacobian, and in either coordinate

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon=c^\varepsilon(	heta)\,d	heta\,dx_\pm.
\]

This is an exact change of variables on the same positive measure.

At fixed \(x_\pm\), the roof derivative is \(e_\pm'\), so the unit-roof-speed fields have densities

\[
 \rho_\pm^\varepsilon=
rac{c^\varepsilon}{|e_\pm'|}.
\]

The pullback Jacobian

\[
 J_h^\pm(y)
 =\frac{\rho_\pm^\varepsilon(\Theta_h^\pm y)}
        {\rho_\pm^\varepsilon(y)}
\]

has the correct orientation for the displayed covariance identity. The absolute speed is retained. I found no missing \(\ell\)-factor or reciprocal error in this coordinate change.

The finite-count pointwise comparison in module 248 disjointizes the source by the first successful endpoint-distance clock. Each admitted part is transported through the exact covariance and bounded by the complete short paired target. The factor two counts the two explicitly chosen comparison directions, not the number of words or chambers. Since the source selector remains at the starting roof and the target comparison is positive, no selector derivative or signed cancellation is needed.

Under the stated schedule the recovered part has height \(O(B^{-1/384})\). The exact positive split

\[
 \mathsf U_B
 =\mathsf V_B+\mathsf U_B^{\rm rem}
\]

is valid at finite count, with \(0\le \mathsf U_B^{\rm rem}\le \mathsf U_B\).

These arguments are coherent within their admitted domain.

## 7. Critical trace and exact zero speed

Module 247 computes the regular nongrazing backward-critical incoming trace as

\[
 f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta)
 =\frac{\omega(q_*)W^\varepsilon(q_*)}
 {4\pi c_*\,e_\perp(\theta)^{\mathsf T}K_*e_\perp(\theta)}.
\]

This formula correctly permits a positive trace. It does not infer that the positive minimum with the outgoing trace has controlled relative variation. That distinction was essential in the previous reports and is preserved.

The exact zero-speed lemma is also appropriately limited. If at least one endpoint derivative is nonzero, the relative speed vanishes at at most one \(s\)-value and is paired-measure null. When both endpoint derivatives vanish on a definable interval, the endpoint roofs are constant there and the source is an explicit positive rectangular pulse. The article does not declare those pulses negligible.

The load-bearing issues for a specialist are the one-sided critical trace convention, the regularity of the physical extension, and the definable classification of the common derivative-zero set. I found no contradiction in the written argument, but these continuum points are not certified by the finite fixtures.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 9. Revision 104: positive angular-interval comparison
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 9. Revision 104: positive angular-interval comparison

Module 250 is the conceptual center of revision 104. It assumes source angular sets \(I_j\), comparison sets \(J_j\), and one-sided interval inclusion. For the positive masses

\[
 C_j=\int_{I_j}c\,d\theta,
 \qquad
 D_j=\int_{J_j}c\,d\theta,
\]

it sets

\[
 \alpha_j=\min\{1,\kappa D_j/C_j\}
\]

when \(C_j>0\).

If the selected source at a roof \(t\) is positive, the product-a.e. inclusion implies that almost every comparison angle contains the appropriate one-sided interval of roofs of length \(r\). Hence

\[
 rD_j
 \le
 \int_{t+\tau_j(0,r)}T_{J_j}(u)\,du,
 \qquad
 \alpha_jT_{H,j}(t)
 \le \alpha_jC_j
 \le\kappa D_j.
\]

Summing and using the physical overlap bound gives

\[
 \sum_j\alpha_jT_{H,j}(t)
 \le
 \frac{N\kappa}{r}
 \int_{t-r}^{t+r}\mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon(u)\,du.
\]

The quantifiers are sound: positivity of the selected integral gives a source set of positive angular measure, and Fubini converts the product-a.e. inclusion into the needed statement for almost every comparison angle. The proof does not require a pointwise map from each source trajectory to a comparison trajectory.

The exact positive remainder satisfies

\[
 (1-\alpha_j)C_j=(C_j-\kappa D_j)_+.
\]

This is the correct deficit. The theorem neither differentiates the positive minimum nor divides by any endpoint or relative speed. It therefore genuinely reaches stationary endpoint geometries missed by the preceding clocks.

The theorem is conditional on the interval inclusion, mass balance and physical overlap. Its strength on the Lorentz family depends entirely on verifying those conditions on a sufficiently complete family.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 10. Stationary-critical arm balance
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 10. Stationary-critical arm balance

On a regular critical arm the incoming roof is constant and

\[
 f_-^\varepsilon(x)=\frac{N_*}{Q_*(x)},
 \qquad
 \lambda_\circ\le Q_*(x)\le\Lambda_\circ.
\]

The outgoing roof is written

\[
 b(x)=a_*+d+\psi(x),
 \qquad 0\le d\le\delta/2,
\]

with three actual reached levels. The source and comparison intervals are

\[
 I=(0,x_1),
 \qquad
 J=(x_2,x_3),
\]

where \(\psi(x_1)=\delta/2\), \(\psi(x_2)=2\delta\), and \(\psi(x_3)=3\delta\).

Writing

\[
 w=\min\{1,f_+^\varepsilon/f_-^\varepsilon\},
 \qquad
 \mu_J=|J|^{-1}\int_Jw,
\]

the estimate

\[
 \frac{\int_Ic^\varepsilon}
      {\int_Jc^\varepsilon}
 \le
 \frac{\Lambda_\circ}{\lambda_\circ\mu_J}
 \frac{x_1}{x_3-x_2}
\]

is correct. Under the elasticity bound

\[
 \frac{x\psi'(x)}{\psi(x)}\le K,
\]

integration of \(\psi'/\psi\) gives

\[
 x_3-x_2
 \ge x_1\frac{\log(3/2)}{K},
\]

and hence the displayed mass balance. No lower bound on \(\psi'\) is needed.

The interval inclusion is also correct: source lengths are at most \(\delta\), comparison lengths are below \(4\delta\), and the outgoing endpoint advances by more than \(\delta\). Disjoint physical arms give overlap one on the pairing-sheet space.

This proves a genuine pointwise height theorem for the certified stationary-critical arm source, including every relative position.

The theorem does not prove that every stationary-critical arm reaches the three levels before a true boundary, has a schedule-compatible level-width ratio, or belongs to a family with a uniform finite-order budget. Finite-count definability alone gives no uniform bound on the order, neighborhood or reach. The author states these limitations correctly.
