revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 7. The finite-count capacity bound
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 7. The finite-count capacity bound

The pool capacities are

\[
P_r(t)=\int Q_rp_\vee\,d\theta,
\qquad
D_r(t)=\int Q_rc^
arepsilon\,d\theta,
\qquad
E_r(t)=\int Q_re_\partial\,d\theta,
\]

with

\[
P_r=D_r+E_r.
\]

For the paired-minimum part, every positively oriented admitted segment contains \([t,t+r]\), and every negatively oriented admitted segment contains \([t-r,t]\). Therefore

\[
D_r(t)
\le
{1\over r}
\int_{t-r}^{t+r}
\mathsf T_\Delta^
arepsilon(u)\,du.
\]

The factor is correct. Each orientation contributes one interval of length \(r\); after the deterministic disjointization the two contributions combine into the single two-sided integral displayed above.

For the endpoint-difference part, the inherited endpoint passage gives

\[
e_\partial(\theta)
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_{a(\theta)}^{b(\theta)}
A(u,\theta)I_m(u,\theta)/z(u,\theta)\,du.
\]

Since every admitted segment lies in \((t-\Delta,t+\Delta)\) and \(Q_r\le1\), one-copy physical summation gives

\[
E_r(t)
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_{t-\Delta}^{t+\Delta}v^0(u)\,du.
\]

I found no hidden block multiplicity in this step. The comparison weight is a single physical-sheet indicator, not a sum over source blocks.

Combining the two estimates yields the asserted finite-count bound

\[
P_r(t)
\le
{1\over r}
\int_{t-r}^{t+r}
\mathsf T_\Delta^
arepsilon(u)\,du
+
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_{t-\Delta}^{t+\Delta}v^0(u)\,du.
\]

Using the inherited fixed-window average inputs gives

\[
\mathcal H_M(KP_r)
\le
CK\{\varepsilon^{1/16}+(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta\}.
\]

The independence of the leading constant from the previously fixed positive window is load-bearing. It is inherited rather than newly proved in revision 108.

Accordingly, statements that source outside the verified comparison subspace is “retained” should be read as follows: it remains in the original positive source before the roofwise allocation, and every unallocated fraction remains in the residual. It is not retained with coefficient one whenever \( eta_{r,K}(t)>0\). The manuscript's certificate definition makes the global roofwise nature of the argument explicit, so this is principally a matter of interpretation and presentation rather than a counterexample to the displayed inequalities.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 10. Domination of revision-107 allocations
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 10. Domination of revision-107 allocations

For a compatible revision-107 family with comparison width at least \(r\), comparison length below \(\Delta\), overlap at most \(N\) and block budget \(\kappa\), every active comparison support contains one of the canonical \(r\)-windows. It is therefore contained in the canonical pool.

The old blockwise allocation satisfies

\[
\beta_jT_j(t)\le\beta_jC_j\le\kappa P_j.
\]

Summing the active blocks and using the full physical overlap gives

\[
V^{\rm old}(t)\le N\kappa P_r(t).
\]

Since source blocks are disjoint and their scalar fractions lie in \([0,1]\), also

\[
V^{\rm old}(t)\le U(t).
\]

Consequently

\[
V^{\rm old}(t)\le V_{r,N\kappa}(t),
\qquad
R_{r,N\kappa}(t)\le U(t)-V^{\rm old}(t).
\]

This is a genuine pointwise dominance statement, not merely a comparison of integrated capacities. I found the use of the inherited common-window lemma and the overlap factor \(N\) correct.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 15. The remaining positive source
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 15. The remaining positive source

The canonical residual can retain positive height for several distinct reasons.

1. The source may concentrate on segments whose residence is smaller than the fixed \(r_B\) at increasing collision counts.

2. The admissible comparison space may exclude singular endpoint extensions for which finite traces, absolute continuity or the weighted variation estimate have not been verified.

3. Even when source and comparison spaces coincide, the pool capacity at the same target roof may be smaller than \(U/K_B\) at the collision-uniform scale.

4. The endpoint envelope may be finite but spatially arranged so that few segments contain a complete one-sided \(r_B\)-window.

5. Flat, short-reach, nonstationary and capacity-deficient microscopic sheets can remain whenever other same-event sheets do not provide enough roofwise capacity.

6. The inherited logarithmic and inverse-residence criteria remain unverified on the full Lorentz source.

The canonical construction removes selection and overlap as independent construction problems. It does not remove physical scarcity.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 16. What a decisive next revision must prove
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 16. What a decisive next revision must prove

A revision capable of changing the recommendation must prove, for an explicit outer schedule \(r_B,\Delta_B,K_B\) fixed before collision limsup,

\[
\lim_{B\to\infty}
\limsup_{m\to\infty}
\sup_{R,n,k}
m^2
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t\in\mathcal C_{m,R,n,k}(M)}
\bigl(
\mathsf U_{B,m}^{\rm micro}(t)
-K_BP_{r_B,m}(t)
\bigr)_+
=0
\]

for every fixed \(M\).

There are several logically acceptable routes, but one of them must be completed on the original source.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ### Route A: a collision-uniform capacity-abundance theorem
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
### Route A: a collision-uniform capacity-abundance theorem

Prove that the canonical pool contains enough same-event endpoint-envelope capacity at a schedule-compatible fixed window, after the complete physical sum and uniformly over radius and exact labels.

This requires more than finite-count coverage. It requires a quantitative lower comparison between the original microscopic source and the pool capacity, with every singular or excluded class either admitted under proved trace hypotheses or estimated separately.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 19. Minor mathematical and expository requests
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 19. Minor mathematical and expository requests

1. In the statement following the restriction to a verified comparison subspace, clarify that the source outside that subspace is retained in the original source but may receive the global roofwise multiplier \( eta_{r,K}(t)\); it is not retained sheetwise with coefficient one.

2. State directly in the maximality theorem that the source allocation is global in the roof variable and is not a coupling between individual source and comparison sheets.

3. In the dominance theorem, include the condition \(r\le r_{
m old}\) in the theorem's displayed hypotheses rather than only in prose as “window width at least \(r\).”

4. In the strictness diagnostic, emphasize in the proposition statement, not only the proof, that the old class has roof-independent source blocks and requires inclusion of the translated entire source interval.

5. Place the exact definition of the admissible comparison subspace in the active article near Definition `def:v108-pool`, rather than referring generally to wherever the inherited regular-segment hypotheses were verified.

6. Record the final v108 workflow states in a later provenance-only commit if they complete, without changing the freeze-time statements in this report.

7. Consolidate current validation metadata so that stale revision-105 headings cannot be mistaken for the active qualification record.

These requests do not alter the principal recommendation.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 1. Recommendation
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revision 109 is a genuine theorem-bearing response to the revision-108 report. It does not add another abstract certificate class and does not merely rename the canonical shortage. Instead, it derives new finite-itinerary optical geometry on the actual Lorentz trajectories, completes one-sided endpoint traces on the inherited physical pairing sheets, distinguishes visited grazing from tangency to an unvisited disk, and pays the complete comparison capacity of the visited-grazing class.

The main new conclusions are the following.

1. The broken-path action has the displayed positive second variation, and stationary elimination gives a uniformly positive reduced endpoint Hessian
   \[
   \lambda_\circ I_2\le D_q^2F\le \Lambda_\circ I_2,
   \qquad
   \lambda_\circ=\frac{9\sqrt{19}}{200},
   \quad
   \Lambda_\circ=\frac{47}{6}.
   \]

2. The endpoint-coordinate density has the exact optical representation
   \[
   \omega=|\partial_{p_0}\alpha_m|^{-1}
   =\frac{|G_{0m}|}{R}
   =\frac{Rc_0c_m}{\mathfrak b_m},
   \]
   where \(\mathfrak b_m\) is the positive \((1,2)\)-entry of the stated free-flight/reflection product.

3. With \(\varrho=47/59\), the manuscript obtains the per-trajectory bounds
   \[
   \omega\le \frac{47}{6}\varrho^{m-1},
   \qquad
   \frac{\omega}{c_j}\le \frac{2209}{72}\varrho^{m-2},
   \]
   and hence
   \[
   \omega I_m\le 500\varrho^{(m-2)_+}.
   \]

4. The Gauss-coordinate differential system gives integrability of \(1/z\) up to both physical ends of every positive-length regular pairing segment. A Schur-complement formula without inverse incidences extends the reduced Hessian continuously when visited incidences tend to zero.

5. The coarea density has finite one-sided endpoint traces and an integrable closed-segment variation bound. If an endpoint limiting trajectory contains an actually visited interior grazing collision, that endpoint trace vanishes and therefore the positive paired minimum on the whole segment is zero.

6. The manuscript correctly distinguishes this from tangency to an unvisited third disk. In the latter case the clearance guard may force \(W^\varepsilon=1\) while all visited incidences and the optical density remain positive, so the endpoint trace need not vanish.

7. The full fixed-window comparison pool can consequently be taken on the complete inherited positive-length physical pairing space. The original source on visited-grazing-ended sheets is zero, but their endpoint-maximum comparison capacity need not be zero. That complete capacity is paid by the original uncut optical volume.

8. If \(\mathsf R_B^{\rm full}\) is the canonical residual using the complete pool and \(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}\) is the residual after removing visited-grazing comparison capacity, then
   \[
   0\le \mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm full}
   \le K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm gr},
   \]
   and
   \[
   \mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm full})
   \le C_MB^{-95/384}.
   \]

I audited the new article, its model and input statements, modules

- `core/260_optical_jacobi_and_endpoint_trace_completion.tex`;
- `core/261_grazing_capacity_payment_and_nongrazing_shortage.tex`;
- `comparison-scope.tex`;
- `RESPONSE_TO_REFEREE.md`;
- `PROOF_LEDGER.md`;
- `SOURCE_MANIFEST.json`;
- `PUBLICATION_STATUS.json`;
- `VALIDATION.md`;

and the controlling revision-108 report. Within the assumptions actually stated in those files, I found no decisive sign error in the second variation, no reversed optical product, no missing incidence factor in the marked estimate, no invalid positive-part subtraction, no exponent-arithmetic error, no hidden word-count factor, and no illegal exchange of the collision limit with the outer parameter.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the revision. The current final reduction is

\[
\mathcal E_M
\le
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng})
+C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

where

\[
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}(t)
=
\bigl(
\mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}(t)
-K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}(t)
\bigr)_+.
\]

The manuscript proves that the unchanged exact-label raw pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng})\longrightarrow0
\qquad
\text{for every fixed }M.
\]

**No theorem establishes this limit.**

The remaining residual includes the full positive weight of the nongrazing microscopic source not paid by the available fixed-window capacity. It can still contain unvisited disk tangencies, nongrazing critical entrances, section-boundary cuts, shrinking flat or short-reach segments, and capacity-deficient sheets. Positivity of every visited endpoint incidence at each fixed collision count does not provide a collision-uniform lower incidence bound. The per-trajectory exponential optical estimate is not a summation theorem over physical trajectories or collision words.

Thus revision 109 completes a real physical component of the scarcity problem, but it does not prove capacity abundance on the remaining physical source. The residual is still the upper pointwise obstruction itself, not a secondary error after the main theorem.

At the requested four-journal benchmark, this is insufficient for acceptance. The new optical and endpoint-trace analysis is technically meaningful, but the paper continues to be organized around a raw pointwise local limit theorem which remains unproved. Nor, in its present specialized form, does the visited-grazing payment constitute a separate theorem of top-four breadth independent of that unfinished endpoint.

## 4. Scope of this review
## 5. The inherited obstruction from revision 108
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 5. The inherited obstruction from revision 108

Revision 108 constructed, at each target roof, the complete admissible fixed-window comparison pool on the then-verified comparison space. It defined

\[
P_r(t)=\int Q_r(t,\theta)p_\vee(\theta)\,d\theta
\]

and allocated the original microscopic source by

\[
V_{r,K}(t)=\min\{U(t),KP_r(t)\},
\qquad
R_{r,K}(t)=(U(t)-KP_r(t))_+.
\]

That construction solved the measurable-selection and overlap problem within its declared scalar certificate class. It did not prove that the pool had enough capacity, uniformly in collision count, to pay the microscopic source.

The revision-108 report therefore asked for a genuine Lorentz-specific scarcity or capacity-abundance theorem in the required limit order. It also identified endpoint-trace completion, singular extensions, and the distinction between source weight and comparison capacity as load-bearing physical issues.

Revision 109 responds to those points in the correct direction. It does not infer abundance from finite-count exhaustion. It proves a physical endpoint theorem and removes one entire physical class from the unresolved capacity question.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 6. Endpoint section cap
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 6. Endpoint section cap

The section test is uniformly separated from grazing at the initial and terminal collisions. The only section centers with tangential coordinate exceeding \(1/2\) in magnitude have coordinate

\[
\frac{2q_R}{1+q_R^2},
\qquad
q_R<\frac{53}{100}.
\]

The manuscript verifies

\[
\frac{2(53/100)}{1+(53/100)^2}+
rac1{200}<
rac9{10}.
\]

Hence on the closure of the original section tests

\[
|p_0|,|p_m|\le\frac9{10},
\qquad
c_0,c_m\ge\frac{\sqrt{19}}{10}.
\]

This is a direct geometric estimate and supplies a genuine uniform endpoint lower incidence without introducing an interior incidence cutoff.

I found no numerical or logical error in this step.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 7. Second variation and reduced endpoint Hessian
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 7. Second variation and reduced endpoint Hessian

For an actual fixed collision itinerary, the manuscript writes

\[
D^2S[\xi,\xi]
=
R\left(c_0\xi_0^2+c_m\xi_m^2
+2\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}c_i\xi_i^2\right)
+
R^2\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}
\frac{(c_i\xi_i+c_{i+1}\xi_{i+1})^2}{\tau_i}.
\]

The signs are consistent with the chosen actual orientation of the circular boundaries and the specular relations at departure and arrival. Every displayed term is nonnegative.

Letting \(H=D^2S\), eliminating the stationary interior variables gives

\[
G
=H_{EE}-H_{EI}H_{II}^{-1}H_{IE},
\]

and the variational characterization

\[
\eta^{\mathsf T}G\eta
=
\min_\zeta
(\eta,\zeta)^{\mathsf T}H(\eta,\zeta).
\]

The explicit endpoint diagonal terms yield

\[
G\ge R\operatorname{diag}(c_0,c_m).
\]

The endpoint section cap then gives the uniform lower bound. Choosing zero interior variation gives the upper bound by the endpoint block. The constant \(47/6\) is conservative but compatible with

\[
R_++\frac{2R_+^2}{\tau_-}=
rac{47}{6}.
\]

I found no decisive defect in this reduction. A specialist should nevertheless check the boundary-orientation convention and the second derivative of each flight directly, because all later sign and positivity statements depend on this formula.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 8. Exact optical denominator and marked incidence
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 8. Exact optical denominator and marked incidence

The manuscript introduces

\[
\mathsf S(s)=
\begin{pmatrix}1&s\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mathsf C(\kappa)=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\kappa&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\kappa_i=\frac{2}{Rc_i},
\]

and

\[
\mathsf M_m
=
\mathsf S(\tau_{m-1})\mathsf C(\kappa_{m-1})
\cdots
\mathsf S(\tau_1)\mathsf C(\kappa_1)
\mathsf S(\tau_0).
\]

The exact identity

\[
\mathfrak b_m=(\mathsf M_m)_{12}
=\prod_i\tau_i\det J
\]

is consistent with the tridiagonal continuant obtained from the interior Hessian. It gives

\[
\omega
=|\partial_{p_0}\alpha_m|^{-1}
=
rac{|G_{0m}|}{R}
=
rac{Rc_0c_m}{\mathfrak b_m}.
\]

All matrix entries are nonnegative. Each interior reflection increases the top component of a positive second column by at least the factor

\[
1+\frac{2\tau_-}{R_+}=
rac{59}{47}.
\]

This yields

\[
\mathfrak b_m\ge\tau_-\left(\frac{59}{47}\right)^{m-1}
\]

and therefore the first optical bound.

For a marked collision \(j\), the coefficient of \(\kappa_j\) splits into positive left and right continuants. The resulting estimate

\[
\mathfrak b_m
\ge
\kappa_j\tau_-^2\left(\frac{59}{47}\right)^{m-2}
\]

implies

\[
\frac{\omega}{c_j}
\le
\frac{R_+^2}{2\tau_-^2}
\left(\frac{47}{59}\right)^{m-2}
=
\frac{2209}{72}
\left(\frac{47}{59}\right)^{m-2}.
\]

The summation

\[
\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}q_0^{d_j}
\le
\frac{2q_0}{1-q_0}
=
rac{47}{3}
\]

then gives the stated bound

\[
\omega I_m\le500\varrho^{(m-2)_+}.
\]

I found the constants and exponent arithmetic consistent. The manuscript also makes the essential restraint explicit: this is a per-trajectory estimate, not a theorem controlling the sum over all collision words or physical sheets. That restraint is mathematically necessary.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 9. Fixed-angle Gauss coordinates and inverse-gradient integrability
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 9. Fixed-angle Gauss coordinates and inverse-gradient integrability

On a constant-angle pairing segment,

\[
\nabla F(q)=ze,
\]

so differentiating in \(z\) gives

\[
\frac{dq}{dz}=G^{-1}e,
\qquad
\frac{du}{dz}=z e^{\mathsf T}G^{-1}e.
\]

The Hessian bounds imply

\[
2\lambda_\circ
\le
\frac{d(z^2)}{du}
\le
2\Lambda_\circ.
\]

Thus \(z\) is strictly increasing with the roof coordinate, the endpoint limits of \(q\) exist in a chosen angular lift, and

\[
\int_a^b\frac{du}{z}
\le
\lambda_\circ^{-1}(z_b-z_a)
\le
\lambda_\circ^{-1}
\min\left\{
\sqrt2R_+,
\sqrt{2\Lambda_\circ(b-a)}
\right\}.
\]

This correctly shows that a critical endpoint of a positive-length segment can occur only at the incoming end.

The derivation is short but coherent. It is one of the strongest additions in revision 109 because it provides the endpoint integrability actually needed by the inherited weighted variation inequality.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 10. Continuous Schur complement at visited grazing
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 10. Continuous Schur complement at visited grazing

The interior Hessian can be factored through

\[
Z=2I+RC_I^{1/2}L_{II}C_I^{1/2}\ge2I.
\]

The reduced Hessian becomes

\[
\begin{aligned}
G={}&RC_E+R^2C_EL_{EE}C_E\\
&-R^3C_EL_{EI}C_I^{1/2}Z^{-1}
C_I^{1/2}L_{IE}C_E.
\end{aligned}
\]

This formula contains no inverse power of an interior incidence. Since \(Z^{-1}\) stays uniformly bounded, it extends continuously when one or several visited incidences tend to zero. The order bounds pass to the limit.

The marked optical estimate further gives \(G_{0m}\to0\) if at least one visited interior incidence tends to zero.

I found this argument internally consistent. It avoids the common error of trying to pass to grazing through a formula containing \(C_I^{-1}\). Independent specialist reconstruction should verify the matrix factorization and the correspondence between the limiting fixed itinerary and the relevant physical endpoint.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 11. Existence of endpoint trajectories and clearances
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 11. Existence of endpoint trajectories and clearances

The manuscript argues one-sidedly from the actual event. The endpoint initial angle and momentum converge. For each designated next disk, the flight quadratic has a continuous entry root up to tangency; the positive finite-horizon flight lower bound prevents collapse. Specular reflection is continuous at tangency. Induction over the finite itinerary therefore gives limits for all visited collision points, velocities, flight lengths, and incidences.

Third-disk clearances also have limits because only finitely many lattice disks can approach a finite-horizon flight and the distance to each is continuous.

This is a plausible and economical endpoint argument. It does not continue a forbidden itinerary past a physical boundary. The most delicate cases are simultaneous endpoint events: a visited grazing together with a third-disk tangency, a section boundary, or another itinerary boundary. The one-sided nature of the construction appears sufficient, but this is a point that should be checked by a human billiards specialist against the precise inherited definition of maximal physical pairing segments.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 12. Coarea trace completion
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 12. Coarea trace completion

The coarea determinant is

\[
\chi
=
\det D_q(F,\arg\nabla F)
=
e^{\perp\mathsf T}Ge^\perp
\ge\lambda_\circ.
\]

Thus

\[
f^\varepsilon
=
\frac{\omega W^\varepsilon}{4\pi c_*\chi}
\]

has finite one-sided limits once the finite trajectory, \(G\), \(\omega\), and the guard variables have one-sided limits.

The inherited regular-point inequality is

\[
|\partial_u f^\varepsilon|
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})AI_m/z.
\]

The new marked optical estimate bounds \(AI_m\) uniformly on each finite trajectory by a constant times \(\varrho^{(m-2)_+}\), while the Gauss-coordinate lemma makes \(1/z\) integrable. Consequently the derivative has an integrable majorant on the closed segment.

Local absolute continuity on compact regular subsegments, the proved endpoint limits, and the integrable derivative bound yield the closed-segment estimate

\[
|f^\varepsilon(b-)-f^\varepsilon(a+)|
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_a^b AI_m/z\,du.
\]

The same calculation gives the one-half-Hölder estimate

\[
|f^\varepsilon(v)-f^\varepsilon(u)|
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\varrho^{(m-2)_+}|v-u|^{1/2}.
\]

Within the inherited regular-point derivative input, this endpoint passage is coherent. It is not an independent reconstruction of the global pairing model or of the regular-point derivative estimate, and the article accurately says so.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 13. Visited grazing and unvisited tangency
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 13. Visited grazing and unvisited tangency

This distinction is essential and is handled correctly in the new text.

If a limiting trajectory contains an actually visited interior grazing collision, then some \(c_j\to0\). The marked estimate gives

\[
\omega\le Cc_j\varrho^{m-2}\longrightarrow0.
\]

Since \(W^\varepsilon\le1\) and \(\chi\ge\lambda_\circ\), the corresponding endpoint trace is zero. The paired density on the whole segment is the minimum of the two endpoint traces, so it is identically zero on that segment.

This conclusion is not based on declaring the grazing set measure zero. It is a pointwise statement about the original positive endpoint minimum.

By contrast, tangency of a flight to an unvisited third disk makes the relevant clearance zero and can force \(W^\varepsilon=1\), but it need not make any visited incidence vanish. The optical density can therefore stay positive. These sheets must remain in the source, and revision 109 retains them.

The report agrees with this distinction.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 14. The full physical comparison pool
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 14. The full physical comparison pool

Revision 109 now takes

\[
\Theta_{\rm ad}=\Theta_{\rm phys}
\]

for all positive-length maximal regular pairing segments of the original exact event. The endpoint trace theorem supplies the previously missing finite traces and variation inequality on this inherited pairing space.

For fixed \(0<r<\Delta\), the deterministic orientation rule defines a Borel pool indicator \(Q_r\le1\). With

\[
P_r=D_r+E_r,
\]

the paired-minimum part satisfies

\[
D_r(t)
\le
\frac1r
\int_{t-r}^{t+r}
\mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon(u)\,du.
\]

The endpoint-difference part satisfies

\[
E_r(t)
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_{t-\Delta}^{t+\Delta}v^0(u)\,du.
\]

Hence

\[
P_r(t)
\le
\frac1r
\int_{t-r}^{t+r}
\mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon(u)\,du
+
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_{t-\Delta}^{t+\Delta}v^0(u)\,du.
\]

This is the same finite-count capacity estimate as in revision 108, now on the complete inherited positive-length comparison space rather than a space restricted by unverified endpoint traces.

The conclusion remains conditional on the inherited global Borel pairing construction, one-copy multiplicity convention, common coarea versions, and averaged analytic estimates. Revision 109 has completed the local endpoint regularity needed to use those inputs; it has not independently re-proved the global inputs.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 15. Zero grazing source and paid grazing capacity
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 15. Zero grazing source and paid grazing capacity

Let \(\Gamma\) be the set of pairing segments whose limiting finite itinerary has a visited interior incidence equal to zero at at least one endpoint. The endpoint incidence limits are Borel, so \(\Gamma\) is Borel.

On \(\Gamma\),

\[
c^\varepsilon=0.
\]

Thus every original selected paired source on \(\Gamma\) is exactly zero at finite count.

However,

\[
p_\vee=e_\partial
\]

on this class, and the comparison capacity need not vanish. The completed variation estimate yields

\[
P_r^{\rm gr}(t)
\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_{t-\Delta}^{t+\Delta}v^0(u)\,du.
\]

After the complete one-copy physical sum and the inherited fixed-window volume estimate,

\[
\mathcal H_M(KP_r^{\rm gr})
\le
CK(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta.
\]

This is a genuine physical payment of the entire visited-grazing comparison capacity. It neither deletes that capacity nor confuses zero source weight with zero endpoint envelope.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 16. Residual comparison and exponent audit
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 16. Residual comparison and exponent audit

Revision 109 chooses

\[
h_B=\frac{\delta(B)}2,
\qquad
r_B=\frac{\delta(B)}8,
\qquad
\Delta_B=8\delta(B),
\qquad
K_B=\max\{1,\varepsilon(B)^{-1/32}\}.
\]

All of these quantities are fixed from the outer parameter before the collision limit.

Since

\[
P_{r_B}=P_{r_B}^{\rm ng}+P_{r_B}^{\rm gr},
\]

the elementary positive-part inequality gives

\[
0
\le
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm full}
\le
K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm gr}.
\]

With \(\Delta_B=O(\varepsilon^4)\) and \(K_B=O(\varepsilon^{-1/32})\),

\[
K_B(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta_B
=O(\varepsilon^{95/32}).
\]

Because \(\varepsilon(B)=A_0B^{-1/12}\), this becomes

\[
O(B^{-95/384}).
\]

The exponent arithmetic is correct.

The accepted complete-pool source has height

\[
O\left(
\varepsilon^{-1/32}
\{\varepsilon^{1/16}+O(\varepsilon^3)\}
\right)
=O(\varepsilon^{1/32})
=O(B^{-1/384}).
\]

Substitution into the inherited scalar reduction gives

\[
\mathcal E_M
\le
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng})
+C_MB^{-1/384}.
\]

I found no defect in this positive decomposition or its order of limits.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 17. The exact remaining obstruction
## 18. Top-four significance
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 18. Top-four significance

The optical and endpoint-trace calculations are nontrivial and useful. In particular, the continuous Schur-complement formula and the exact distinction between visited grazing and unvisited tangency clarify a genuine technical obstruction in the preceding revisions.

Nevertheless, the requested benchmark is not met.

First, the paper's organizing theorem remains unproved. The final residual limit is explicitly equivalent to the desired upper pointwise law.

Second, the new theorem removes one physical component whose original paired source is already zero, although its comparison capacity must be paid. This is important for the correctness of the canonical allocation, but it does not yet control the positive nongrazing source which carries the remaining theorem.

Third, the result remains highly specialized to one finite-horizon triangular Lorentz family, one section, one guard, one exact-label event, and a long inherited analytic pipeline. Revision 109 does not extract a general theorem about endpoint traces or capacity scarcity for a broad class of singular hyperbolic systems.

Fourth, the continuum proof chain still relies on 259 inherited modules and several load-bearing inputs which have not received an independent human specialist audit.

Accordingly, the new material strengthens the project but does not justify publication in *Annals*, *Acta*, *Inventiones*, or *JAMS* in its present form.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revision 109 is a genuine theorem-bearing response to the revision-108 report. It does not add another abstract certificate class and does not merely rename the canonical shortage. Instead, it derives new finite-itinerary optical geometry on the actual Lorentz trajectories, completes one-sided endpoint traces on the inherited physical pairing sheets, distinguishes visited grazing from tangency to an unvisited disk, and pays the complete comparison capacity of the visited-grazing class.

The main new conclusions are the following.

1. The broken-path action has the displayed positive second variation, and stationary elimination gives a uniformly positive reduced endpoint Hessian
   \[
   \lambda_\circ I_2\le D_q^2F\le \Lambda_\circ I_2,
   \qquad
   \lambda_\circ=\frac{9\sqrt{19}}{200},
   \quad
   \Lambda_\circ=\frac{47}{6}.
   \]

2. The endpoint-coordinate density has the exact optical representation
   \[
   \omega=|\partial_{p_0}\alpha_m|^{-1}
   =\frac{|G_{0m}|}{R}
   =\frac{Rc_0c_m}{\mathfrak b_m},
   \]
   where \(\mathfrak b_m\) is the positive \((1,2)\)-entry of the stated free-flight/reflection product.

3. With \(\varrho=47/59\), the manuscript obtains the per-trajectory bounds
   \[
   \omega\le \frac{47}{6}\varrho^{m-1},
   \qquad
   \frac{\omega}{c_j}\le \frac{2209}{72}\varrho^{m-2},
   \]
   and hence
   \[
   \omega I_m\le 500\varrho^{(m-2)_+}.
   \]

4. The Gauss-coordinate differential system gives integrability of \(1/z\) up to both physical ends of every positive-length regular pairing segment. A Schur-complement formula without inverse incidences extends the reduced Hessian continuously when visited incidences tend to zero.

5. The coarea density has finite one-sided endpoint traces and an integrable closed-segment variation bound. If an endpoint limiting trajectory contains an actually visited interior grazing collision, that endpoint trace vanishes and therefore the positive paired minimum on the whole segment is zero.

6. The manuscript correctly distinguishes this from tangency to an unvisited third disk. In the latter case the clearance guard may force \(W^\varepsilon=1\) while all visited incidences and the optical density remain positive, so the endpoint trace need not vanish.

7. The full fixed-window comparison pool can consequently be taken on the complete inherited positive-length physical pairing space. The original source on visited-grazing-ended sheets is zero, but their endpoint-maximum comparison capacity need not be zero. That complete capacity is paid by the original uncut optical volume.

8. If \(\mathsf R_B^{\rm full}\) is the canonical residual using the complete pool and \(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}\) is the residual after removing visited-grazing comparison capacity, then
   \[
   0\le \mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm full}
   \le K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm gr},
   \]
   and
   \[
   \mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm full})
   \le C_MB^{-95/384}.
   \]

I audited the new article, its model and input statements, modules

- `core/260_optical_jacobi_and_endpoint_trace_completion.tex`;
- `core/261_grazing_capacity_payment_and_nongrazing_shortage.tex`;
- `comparison-scope.tex`;
- `RESPONSE_TO_REFEREE.md`;
- `PROOF_LEDGER.md`;
- `SOURCE_MANIFEST.json`;
- `PUBLICATION_STATUS.json`;
- `VALIDATION.md`;

and the controlling revision-108 report. Within the assumptions actually stated in those files, I found no decisive sign error in the second variation, no reversed optical product, no missing incidence factor in the marked estimate, no invalid positive-part subtraction, no exponent-arithmetic error, no hidden word-count factor, and no illegal exchange of the collision limit with the outer parameter.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the revision. The current final reduction is

\[
\mathcal E_M
\le
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng})
+C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

where

\[
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}(t)
=
\bigl(
\mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}(t)
-K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}(t)
\bigr)_+.
\]

The manuscript proves that the unchanged exact-label raw pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng})\longrightarrow0
\qquad
\text{for every fixed }M.
\]

**No theorem establishes this limit.**

The remaining residual includes the full positive weight of the nongrazing microscopic source not paid by the available fixed-window capacity. It can still contain unvisited disk tangencies, nongrazing critical entrances, section-boundary cuts, shrinking flat or short-reach segments, and capacity-deficient sheets. Positivity of every visited endpoint incidence at each fixed collision count does not provide a collision-uniform lower incidence bound. The per-trajectory exponential optical estimate is not a summation theorem over physical trajectories or collision words.

Thus revision 109 completes a real physical component of the scarcity problem, but it does not prove capacity abundance on the remaining physical source. The residual is still the upper pointwise obstruction itself, not a secondary error after the main theorem.

At the requested four-journal benchmark, this is insufficient for acceptance. The new optical and endpoint-trace analysis is technically meaningful, but the paper continues to be organized around a raw pointwise local limit theorem which remains unproved. Nor, in its present specialized form, does the visited-grazing payment constitute a separate theorem of top-four breadth independent of that unfinished endpoint.

## 5. The inherited obstruction from revision 108

Revision 108 constructed, at each target roof, the complete admissible fixed-window comparison pool on the then-verified comparison space. It defined

\[
P_r(t)=\int Q_r(t,\theta)p_\vee(\theta)\,d\theta
\]

and allocated the original microscopic source by

\[

\]

That construction solved the measurable-selection and overlap problem within its declared scalar certificate class. It did not prove that the pool had enough capacity, uniformly in collision count, to pay the microscopic source.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 8. Exact optical denominator and marked incidence

The manuscript introduces

\[
\mathsf S(s)=
\begin{pmatrix}1&s\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mathsf C(\kappa)=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\kappa&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\kappa_i=\frac{2}{Rc_i},
\]

and

\[
\mathsf M_m
=
\mathsf S(\tau_{m-1})\mathsf C(\kappa_{m-1})
\cdots
\mathsf S(\tau_1)\mathsf C(\kappa_1)
\mathsf S(\tau_0).
\]

The exact identity

\[
\mathfrak b_m=(\mathsf M_m)_{12}
=\prod_i\tau_i\det J
\]

is consistent with the tridiagonal continuant obtained from the interior Hessian. It gives

\[
\omega
=|\partial_{p_0}\alpha_m|^{-1}
=
rac{|G_{0m}|}{R}
=
rac{Rc_0c_m}{\mathfrak b_m}.
\]

All matrix entries are nonnegative. Each interior reflection increases the top component of a positive second column by at least the factor

\[
1+\frac{2\tau_-}{R_+}=
rac{59}{47}.
\]

This yields

\[
\mathfrak b_m\ge\tau_-\left(\frac{59}{47}\right)^{m-1}
\]

and therefore the first optical bound.

For a marked collision \(j\), the coefficient of \(\kappa_j\) splits into positive left and right continuants. The resulting estimate

\[
\mathfrak b_m
\ge
\kappa_j\tau_-^2\left(\frac{59}{47}\right)^{m-2}
\]

implies

\[
\frac{\omega}{c_j}
\le
\frac{R_+^2}{2\tau_-^2}
\left(\frac{47}{59}\right)^{m-2}
=
\frac{2209}{72}
\left(\frac{47}{59}\right)^{m-2}.
\]

The summation

\[
\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}q_0^{d_j}
\le
\frac{2q_0}{1-q_0}
=
rac{47}{3}
\]

then gives the stated bound

\[
\omega I_m\le500\varrho^{(m-2)_+}.
\]

I found the constants and exponent arithmetic consistent. The manuscript also makes the essential restraint explicit: this is a per-trajectory estimate, not a theorem controlling the sum over all collision words or physical sheets. That restraint is mathematically necessary.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 11. Existence of endpoint trajectories and clearances

The manuscript argues one-sidedly from the actual event. The endpoint initial angle and momentum converge. For each designated next disk, the flight quadratic has a continuous entry root up to tangency; the positive finite-horizon flight lower bound prevents collapse. Specular reflection is continuous at tangency. Induction over the finite itinerary therefore gives limits for all visited collision points, velocities, flight lengths, and incidences.

Third-disk clearances also have limits because only finitely many lattice disks can approach a finite-horizon flight and the distance to each is continuous.

This is a plausible and economical endpoint argument. It does not continue a forbidden itinerary past a physical boundary. The most delicate cases are simultaneous endpoint events: a visited grazing together with a third-disk tangency, a section boundary, or another itinerary boundary. The one-sided nature of the construction appears sufficient, but this is a point that should be checked by a human billiards specialist against the precise inherited definition of maximal physical pairing segments.

\]

This is a genuine physical payment of the entire visited-grazing comparison capacity. It neither deletes that capacity nor confuses zero source weight with zero endpoint envelope.

## 21. Requested clarifications and presentation revisions

The current exposition is substantially clearer than the accumulated shell used in revision 108. I nevertheless recommend the following changes in any further submission.

1. State in the introduction, before the main positive results, the exact residual limit which remains unproved.
2. Avoid using “capacity abundance” without the qualifier “visited-grazing component” in prose, since abundance on the nongrazing source is the missing theorem.
3. Keep the distinction between zero original source and nonzero comparison capacity prominent.
4. State explicitly whether the constant in the one-half-Hölder estimate is uniform over all fixed-count sheets and which inherited constants it uses.
5. Add a short matrix derivation of the corner cofactor identity, rather than referring only to successive determinant expansion.
6. State the one-sided endpoint-limit lemma separately for simultaneous boundary mechanisms.
7. Explain explicitly that \(\Gamma\) can include several grazing incidences and that the proof remains unchanged.
8. Preserve the statement that unvisited third-disk tangencies are retained with their original positive weight.
9. Keep the scalar roofwise allocation distinguished from an individual-sheet coupling.
10. Update the active validation record only from actual completed exact-SHA runs; do not infer success from the workflow definition.
11. Continue to preserve the controlling report's freeze-time CI status even if the jobs later succeed.
12. Do not promote denominator, likelihood, or unrestricted conditional-law conclusions before the scalar residual is closed.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 24. Final recommendation
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 24. Final recommendation

Revision 109 makes genuine and technically credible progress. Within its stated inherited inputs, I found no decisive error in the new optical denominator, marked-incidence estimate, Gauss-coordinate integrability, continuous Schur complement, endpoint trace completion, visited-grazing source identity, grazing-capacity payment, or residual exponent calculation.

The revision nevertheless leaves the exact remaining theorem as

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng})\to0,
\]

and proves no estimate implying it. The paper's principal raw pointwise local limit theorem is therefore still unproved.

**Recommendation at the requested top-four mathematics benchmark: reject in the present form.**

A materially different assessment would require a collision-uniform theorem closing the nongrazing microscopic shortage, or a new general theorem of independent top-four scope whose validity and significance do not depend on that unfinished endpoint.

all_original_sections.original_text:
## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revision 110 is a genuine theorem-bearing response to the revision-109 report. It does not merely introduce another comparison certificate, relabel the nongrazing residual, or replace the original pointwise objective by an averaged statement. It acts directly on the original positive microscopic source and proves a new finite-count payment for a positive submeasure of that source.

The central new decomposition is the following. On each complete physical pairing segment, let

\[
\mathcal V^\varepsilon(\theta)
  =\operatorname{Var}_{[a(\theta),b(\theta)]}
       f^\varepsilon(\cdot,\theta)
\]

be the total variation of the original weighted density, and let

\[
c^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\min\{f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta),f^\varepsilon(b-,\theta)\}
\]

be the original paired coefficient. For an outer multiplier \(\gamma\ge1\), the revision splits

\[
c^\varepsilon
 =c_{\rm var}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
  +c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma},
\]

where

\[
c_{\rm var}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
 =\min\{c^\varepsilon,\gamma\mathcal V^\varepsilon\},
\qquad
c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
 =(c^\varepsilon-\gamma\mathcal V^\varepsilon)_+.
\]

The first term is a genuine positive submeasure of the original source. It is not an endpoint-current difference, a signed Jordan component, a comparison capacity, or a density with a changed normalization.

Using the closed-segment absolute continuity established in revision 109, revision 110 proves

\[
\mathcal V^\varepsilon(\theta)
 \le C_{\rm reg}(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
       \int_{a(\theta)}^{b(\theta)}
       \frac{A(u,\theta)I_m(u,\theta)}{z(u,\theta)}\,du.
\]

It then performs the complete one-copy physical sum before taking any norm. If the selected segment contains the original target roof \(t\) and has length below \(h\), the entire segment lies in \((t-h,t+h)\). Consequently

\[
T_{H,\rm var}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}(t)
 \le C_{\rm reg}\gamma(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
       \int_{t-h}^{t+h}v^0(u)\,du.
\]

At the stated outer schedule

\[
 h_B=\delta(B)/2,
 \qquad
 \gamma_B=\max\{2,\varepsilon(B)^{-1/32}\},
\]

this gives

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm var})
 \le C_MB^{-95/384}.
\]

This is a substantive positive-source estimate. It does not use a lower residence cutoff, an endpoint-speed lower bound, an angular continuation corridor, a selected comparison family, or an unweighted count of collision words.

The revision also proves a useful physical description of the complementary coefficient. If

\[
c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}>0,
\]

then the original density is nearly constant on the whole closed segment:

\[
|f^\varepsilon(u,\theta)-c^\varepsilon(\theta)|
 <\gamma^{-1}c^\varepsilon(\theta).
\]

In particular the original guard remains positive at every point of the segment. At each point at least one original incidence or clearance test lies below its doubled guard threshold, although the witnessing test may vary along the segment. Conversely, if the original guard vanishes at even one point of the closed segment, the whole paired coefficient is assigned to the paid variation part.

Finally, keeping the full original nongrazing comparison pool, the manuscript obtains the exact positive identity

\[
\mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}
 =\mathsf U_B^{\rm var}
  +\min\{\mathsf U_B^{\rm per},K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}\}
  +\mathsf R_B^{\rm per},
\]

where

\[
\mathsf R_B^{\rm per}
 =\bigl(\mathsf U_B^{\rm per}-K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}\bigr)_+.
\]

The old and new shortages satisfy

\[
0\le
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm per}
\le
\mathsf U_B^{\rm var},
\]

and hence

\[
\mathcal H_M(
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm per})
 \le C_MB^{-95/384}.
\]

I audited the newly landed material

- `core/262_positive_variation_payment.tex`;
- `core/263_persistent_guard_and_nongrazing_shortage.tex`;
- `core/264_optical_cofactors_and_simultaneous_endpoints.tex`;
- the revised article shell;
- `RESPONSE_TO_REFEREE.md`;
- `PROOF_LEDGER.md`;
- `SOURCE_MANIFEST.json`;
- `PUBLICATION_STATUS.json`;
- `VALIDATION.md`;
- the retained revision-109 optical and endpoint modules needed by the new proof; and
- the controlling revision-109 report.

Within the assumptions actually stated in those files, I found no decisive sign error, no invalid positive-source subtraction, no missing factor of the roof-window length, no exponent-arithmetic error, no hidden differentiation of the selector, no word-count multiplier, and no illegal exchange of the collision limit with an outer scale. The total-variation payment, persistence implication, positive-part comparison, signed corner cofactor, multi-mark optical expansion, and simultaneous-endpoint passage are internally coherent.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the revision. The final scalar theorem is

\[
\mathcal E_M
 \le
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm per})
 +C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

and the manuscript proves that the unchanged exact-label raw pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm per})\longrightarrow0
\qquad
\text{for every fixed }M.
\]

**No theorem establishes this limit.**

The revision proves that every surviving source coefficient lies on a short nongrazing segment with nearly constant positive density and a persistent original guard. It does not prove that the ordered pointwise height of those coefficients is small. A positive density can remain essentially constant on an arbitrarily short segment while retaining a large pointwise value. The fixed-window volume estimates control an integral or a paid variation component; they do not by themselves control this remaining amplitude.

The full nongrazing comparison pool may also remain capacity-deficient at the prescribed, collision-independent window. Neither the per-itinerary multi-mark bound nor the existence of a bad guard witness at every roof point supplies a collision-uniform summation theorem over the physical pairing family.

Thus revision 110 proves another real physical component of the scarcity problem, but the persistent guarded shortage remains the upper pointwise obstruction itself. It is not a harmless secondary error after the main theorem.

At the requested four-journal benchmark, this is insufficient for acceptance. The new decomposition and optical refinements are technically meaningful, but the article continues to be organized around an exact-label raw pointwise local limit theorem which remains unproved. Nor, in its present highly specialized form, does the variation payment by itself constitute a separate theorem of top-four breadth independent of that unfinished endpoint.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 6. Borel total variation and closed-segment payment
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 6. Borel total variation and closed-segment payment

Module 262 defines

\[
\mathcal V^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\operatorname{Var}_{[a(\theta),b(\theta)]}
     f^\varepsilon(\cdot,\theta).
\]

The measurability argument is appropriate. After pulling each physical segment back to \([0,1]\), continuity in the segment variable permits computation of variation using finite rational partitions. The variation is therefore a countable supremum of Borel functions.

Because revision 109 established absolute continuity on the closed segment,

\[
\mathcal V^\varepsilon
 =\int_a^b|\partial_u f^\varepsilon|\,du.
\]

The inherited regular derivative input gives

\[
\mathcal V^\varepsilon
 \le C_{\rm reg}(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
       \int_a^b AI_m/z\,du.
\]

This is stronger than an endpoint-difference estimate. A function may return to the same endpoint value while varying substantially in the interior; the manuscript pays the full variation.

For a selected segment of length below \(h\) containing \(t\), the inclusion

\[
(a,b)\subset(t-h,t+h)
\]

is exact. Multiplication by the original selector is harmless because the selector remains at the starting roof and lies in \([0,1]\). Summing the resulting nonnegative integrals over the complete physical pairing space before taking a norm is the correct order. The inherited one-copy coarea identity then gives the finite-count payment by \(v^0\).

I found no hidden number-of-sheets factor in this argument.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 7. The outer schedule and rate
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 7. The outer schedule and rate

With

\[
\gamma_B=O(\varepsilon^{-1/32}),
\qquad
h_B=O(\varepsilon^4),
\]

the payment is

\[
O\bigl(
\varepsilon^{-1/32}
(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\varepsilon^4
\bigr)
 =O(\varepsilon^{95/32}).
\]

Since \(\varepsilon(B)=A_0B^{-1/12}\), this is

\[
O(B^{-95/384}).
\]

The exponent arithmetic is correct. The widths and multiplier are chosen from the outer parameter before the physical sum, uniform norms, and collision limsup.

The rate is much faster than the inherited \(B^{-1/384}\) budget. It can therefore be absorbed without changing the governing error scale.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 8. Persistence of the original guard
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 8. Persistence of the original guard

If

\[
c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}>0,
\]

then

\[
c^\varepsilon>\gamma\mathcal V^\varepsilon.
\]

An endpoint attains \(c^\varepsilon\), and total variation bounds the change from that endpoint to every point of the closed segment. Hence

\[
|f^\varepsilon(u)-c^\varepsilon|
 \le\mathcal V^\varepsilon
 <\gamma^{-1}c^\varepsilon.
\]

This proves strict positivity of the weighted density throughout the segment.

On the nongrazing class, the optical factor is finite and positive on the closed segment, including a critical incoming endpoint with fixed Gauss direction. Thus \(f^\varepsilon>0\) implies \(W^\varepsilon>0\).

Because every guard factor lies in \([0,1]\) and equals one once its normalized argument is at least two, \(W^\varepsilon>0\) implies that at least one original incidence or clearance test is below its doubled threshold. The witness may vary with the roof coordinate, as the manuscript correctly states.

Conversely, if the guard vanishes at one point, then the weighted density vanishes there. The total variation from an endpoint attaining the positive paired minimum is at least the minimum itself, so the whole coefficient is paid by the variation part. This implication is correct.

The result is a useful necessary condition for the unresolved source. It is not a smallness theorem for that source.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 9. Exact residual comparison
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 9. Exact residual comparison

Set

\[
U=\mathsf U_B^{\rm per},
\qquad
Y=K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}.
\]

Then

\[
U=\min\{U,Y\}+(U-Y)_+.
\]

Combining this identity with

\[
\mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}
 =\mathsf U_B^{\rm var}
 +\mathsf U_B^{\rm per}
\]

gives the displayed three-term source decomposition.

Moreover, the positive-part map is monotone and one-Lipschitz. Since

\[
\mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}
 =\mathsf U_B^{\rm per}+\mathsf U_B^{\rm var},
\]

one obtains

\[
0\le
(\mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}-Y)_+
 -(\mathsf U_B^{\rm per}-Y)_+
\le
\mathsf U_B^{\rm var}.
\]

This is exactly the claimed comparison between \(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}\) and \(\mathsf R_B^{\rm per}\).

The full nongrazing comparison pool is retained. It is not restricted to the persistent source class, and already-paid sheets may still supply scalar roofwise capacity. This is consistent with the earlier canonical allocation framework.

all_original_sections.original_text: ## 10. Optical appendix

all_original_sections.heading: ### 10.1. Signed corner cofactor
### 10.2. Positive multi-mark expansion
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 10.2. Positive multi-mark expansion

Expanding

\[
\mathsf C(\kappa)=I+\kappa E
\]

inside the optical product gives the positive polynomial

\[
\mathfrak b_m
 =\sum_{S\subset\{1,\ldots,m-1\}}
   \left(\prod_{j\in S}\kappa_j\right)
   \prod_{\nu=0}^{|S|}T_{j_\nu,j_{\nu+1}}.
\]

All coefficients are positive. Retaining the unmarked reflection factors and factoring the coefficient of a prescribed marked set into intervening optical blocks gives

\[
\frac{\omega}{\prod_{j\in S}c_j}
 \le
\frac{R_+^{|S|+1}}
 {2^{|S|}\tau_-^{|S|+1}}
\varrho^{m-|S|-1}.
\]

The formula specializes correctly to the zero-mark and one-mark estimates. The manuscript appropriately restricts the conclusion to a fixed finite itinerary and does not sum it over collision words without a separate weighted-complexity theorem.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 10.3. Simultaneous endpoints
all_original_sections.original_text:
### 10.3. Simultaneous endpoints

The whole-approach endpoint argument is clearer in revision 110. Gauss-coordinate control gives a full one-sided limit, not merely a subsequential one. The designated entry root is continuous up to tangency, the flight lower bound prevents collapse, and the reflection map is continuous at tangency. Finite horizon reduces possible nearby third-disk centers to a finite set, so the clearance minimum also has a limit.

This treats simultaneous visited grazing, unvisited tangency, a section boundary, and a critical incoming endpoint without continuing the event beyond its physical boundary.

all_original_sections.heading: ### 10.4. Uniform trace modulus
## 11. The decisive remaining obstruction
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 11. The decisive remaining obstruction

The required estimate is

\[
\lim_{B\to\infty}
\limsup_{m\to\infty}
\sup_{R,n,k}m^2
\esssup_{t\in\mathcal C_{m,R,n,k}(M)}
\bigl(
\mathsf U_{B,m}^{\rm per}(t)
 -K_BP_{r_B,m}^{\rm ng}(t)
\bigr)_+=0.
\]

Revision 110 does not prove this statement.

The new persistence theorem says that every surviving segment has:

1. positive nongrazing optical density;
2. relative oscillation below \(\gamma_B^{-1}\);
3. the original guard active at every roof point; and
4. at least one small original incidence or clearance test at each roof point.

These are strong structural restrictions, but they do not control pointwise height. A nearly constant coefficient of size one supported on a segment of length \(h_B\) has small roof mass but can retain order-one pointwise height. The inherited uncut volume estimate pays variation; it does not rule out such an almost-flat spike.

Nor does the pointwise existence of a guard witness produce a uniform physical summation. There are \(O(m)\) possible incidence and clearance tests, their thresholds depend on depth, and the witness may change along the segment. A future proof must control the complete family without multiplying a per-itinerary estimate by an uncontrolled number of words or sheets.

The nongrazing pool may also have insufficient fixed-window capacity at the prescribed \(r_B\). The manuscript has not shown that persistent source height is bounded by that capacity, nor that the capacity shortage is rare in the essential-roof topology.

This is the exact point at which the main theorem remains open in the manuscript.

all_original_sections.heading: ## 12. What a decisive next revision must prove
all_original_sections.original_text:
## 12. What a decisive next revision must prove

A revision capable of changing the recommendation must close the displayed persistent-shortage limit. Merely producing another positive split or another certificate class will not suffice unless it yields the required collision-uniform pointwise estimate.

Several routes remain logically possible.

all_original_sections.heading: ### Route A: persistent-segment scarcity
all_original_sections.original_text:
### Route A: persistent-segment scarcity

Prove a physically summed theorem showing that segments with

\[
\mathcal V^
arepsilon<c^
arepsilon/\gamma_B
\]

and an active original guard at every roof point have vanishing ordered height. Such a theorem would need a collision-uniform packing, multiplicity, or weighted-complexity estimate in the original essential-roof topology.

all_original_sections.heading: ### Route B: fixed-window capacity abundance
all_original_sections.original_text:
### Route B: fixed-window capacity abundance

Prove that the complete nongrazing canonical pool has enough capacity at the prescribed outer window to pay the persistent source, up to a term of vanishing ordered height.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revision 110 is a genuine theorem-bearing response to the revision-109 report. It does not merely introduce another comparison certificate, relabel the nongrazing residual, or replace the original pointwise objective by an averaged statement. It acts directly on the original positive microscopic source and proves a new finite-count payment for a positive submeasure of that source.

The central new decomposition is the following. On each complete physical pairing segment, let

\[
\mathcal V^\varepsilon(\theta)
  =\operatorname{Var}_{[a(\theta),b(\theta)]}
       f^\varepsilon(\cdot,\theta)
\]

be the total variation of the original weighted density, and let

\[
c^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\min\{f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta),f^\varepsilon(b-,\theta)\}
\]

be the original paired coefficient. For an outer multiplier \(\gamma\ge1\), the revision splits

\[
c^\varepsilon
 =c_{\rm var}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
  +c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma},
\]

where

\[
c_{\rm var}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
 =\min\{c^\varepsilon,\gamma\mathcal V^\varepsilon\},
\qquad
c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
 =(c^\varepsilon-\gamma\mathcal V^\varepsilon)_+.
\]

The first term is a genuine positive submeasure of the original source. It is not an endpoint-current difference, a signed Jordan component, a comparison capacity, or a density with a changed normalization.

Using the closed-segment absolute continuity established in revision 109, revision 110 proves

\[
\mathcal V^\varepsilon(\theta)
 \le C_{\rm reg}(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
       \int_{a(\theta)}^{b(\theta)}
       \frac{A(u,\theta)I_m(u,\theta)}{z(u,\theta)}\,du.
\]

It then performs the complete one-copy physical sum before taking any norm. If the selected segment contains the original target roof \(t\) and has length below \(h\), the entire segment lies in \((t-h,t+h)\). Consequently

\[
T_{H,\rm var}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}(t)
 \le C_{\rm reg}\gamma(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
       \int_{t-h}^{t+h}v^0(u)\,du.
\]

At the stated outer schedule

\[
 h_B=\delta(B)/2,
 \qquad
 \gamma_B=\max\{2,\varepsilon(B)^{-1/32}\},
\]

this gives

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B^{\rm var})
 \le C_MB^{-95/384}.
\]

This is a substantive positive-source estimate. It does not use a lower residence cutoff, an endpoint-speed lower bound, an angular continuation corridor, a selected comparison family, or an unweighted count of collision words.

The revision also proves a useful physical description of the complementary coefficient. If

\[
c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}>0,
\]

then the original density is nearly constant on the whole closed segment:

\[
|f^\varepsilon(u,\theta)-c^\varepsilon(\theta)|
 <\gamma^{-1}c^\varepsilon(\theta).
\]

In particular the original guard remains positive at every point of the segment. At each point at least one original incidence or clearance test lies below its doubled guard threshold, although the witnessing test may vary along the segment. Conversely, if the original guard vanishes at even one point of the closed segment, the whole paired coefficient is assigned to the paid variation part.

Finally, keeping the full original nongrazing comparison pool, the manuscript obtains the exact positive identity

\[
\mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}
 =\mathsf U_B^{\rm var}
  +\min\{\mathsf U_B^{\rm per},K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}\}
  +\mathsf R_B^{\rm per},
\]

where

\[
\mathsf R_B^{\rm per}
 =\bigl(\mathsf U_B^{\rm per}-K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}\bigr)_+.
\]

The old and new shortages satisfy

\[
0\le
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm per}
\le
\mathsf U_B^{\rm var},
\]

and hence

\[
\mathcal H_M(
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}-\mathsf R_B^{\rm per})
 \le C_MB^{-95/384}.
\]

I audited the newly landed material

- `core/262_positive_variation_payment.tex`;
- `core/263_persistent_guard_and_nongrazing_shortage.tex`;
- `core/264_optical_cofactors_and_simultaneous_endpoints.tex`;
- the revised article shell;
- `RESPONSE_TO_REFEREE.md`;
- `PROOF_LEDGER.md`;
- `SOURCE_MANIFEST.json`;
- `PUBLICATION_STATUS.json`;
- `VALIDATION.md`;
- the retained revision-109 optical and endpoint modules needed by the new proof; and
- the controlling revision-109 report.

Within the assumptions actually stated in those files, I found no decisive sign error, no invalid positive-source subtraction, no missing factor of the roof-window length, no exponent-arithmetic error, no hidden differentiation of the selector, no word-count multiplier, and no illegal exchange of the collision limit with an outer scale. The total-variation payment, persistence implication, positive-part comparison, signed corner cofactor, multi-mark optical expansion, and simultaneous-endpoint passage are internally coherent.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the revision. The final scalar theorem is

\[
\mathcal E_M
 \le
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm per})
 +C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

and the manuscript proves that the unchanged exact-label raw pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm per})\longrightarrow0
\qquad
\text{for every fixed }M.
\]

**No theorem establishes this limit.**

The revision proves that every surviving source coefficient lies on a short nongrazing segment with nearly constant positive density and a persistent original guard. It does not prove that the ordered pointwise height of those coefficients is small. A positive density can remain essentially constant on an arbitrarily short segment while retaining a large pointwise value. The fixed-window volume estimates control an integral or a paid variation component; they do not by themselves control this remaining amplitude.

The full nongrazing comparison pool may also remain capacity-deficient at the prescribed, collision-independent window. Neither the per-itinerary multi-mark bound nor the existence of a bad guard witness at every roof point supplies a collision-uniform summation theorem over the physical pairing family.

Thus revision 110 proves another real physical component of the scarcity problem, but the persistent guarded shortage remains the upper pointwise obstruction itself. It is not a harmless secondary error after the main theorem.

At the requested four-journal benchmark, this is insufficient for acceptance. The new decomposition and optical refinements are technically meaningful, but the article continues to be organized around an exact-label raw pointwise local limit theorem which remains unproved. Nor, in its present highly specialized form, does the variation payment by itself constitute a separate theorem of top-four breadth independent of that unfinished endpoint.

## 5. The inherited obstruction from revision 109

Revision 109 had reduced the original pointwise problem to

\[
\mathcal E_M
 \le
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng})
 +C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

with

\[
\mathsf R_B^{\rm ng}(t)
 =\bigl(
 \mathsf U_B^{\rm micro}(t)
 -K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}(t)
 \bigr)_+.
\]

It had already proved:

- a uniformly positive reduced endpoint Hessian;
- an exact positive optical denominator;
- one-mark inverse-incidence bounds;
- integrability of the inverse gradient in Gauss coordinates;
- finite one-sided endpoint traces;
- zero paired source on visited-grazing-ended segments;
- payment of their complete comparison capacity; and
- the distinction between visited grazing and tangency to an unvisited third disk.

The revision-109 report emphasized that the remaining nongrazing shortage could still contain unvisited tangencies, nongrazing critical entrances, section-boundary cuts, shrinking flat or short-reach segments, and capacity-deficient physical sheets.

Revision 110 acts on that correct remaining source. It does not change the section, guard, labels, normalization, central roof sets, or essential-height topology.

revision_or_obstruction_sections.heading: ## 11. The decisive remaining obstruction
revision_or_obstruction_sections.original_text:
## 11. The decisive remaining obstruction

The required estimate is

\[
\lim_{B\to\infty}
\limsup_{m\to\infty}
\sup_{R,n,k}m^2
\esssup_{t\in\mathcal C_{m,R,n,k}(M)}
\bigl(
\mathsf U_{B,m}^{\rm per}(t)
 -K_BP_{r_B,m}^{\rm ng}(t)
\bigr)_+=0.
\]

Revision 110 does not prove this statement.

The new persistence theorem says that every surviving segment has:

1. positive nongrazing optical density;
2. relative oscillation below \(\gamma_B^{-1}\);
3. the original guard active at every roof point; and
4. at least one small original incidence or clearance test at each roof point.

These are strong structural restrictions, but they do not control pointwise height. A nearly constant coefficient of size one supported on a segment of length \(h_B\) has small roof mass but can retain order-one pointwise height. The inherited uncut volume estimate pays variation; it does not rule out such an almost-flat spike.

Nor does the pointwise existence of a guard witness produce a uniform physical summation. There are \(O(m)\) possible incidence and clearance tests, their thresholds depend on depth, and the witness may change along the segment. A future proof must control the complete family without multiplying a per-itinerary estimate by an uncontrolled number of words or sheets.

The nongrazing pool may also have insufficient fixed-window capacity at the prescribed \(r_B\). The manuscript has not shown that persistent source height is bounded by that capacity, nor that the capacity shortage is rare in the essential-roof topology.

This is the exact point at which the main theorem remains open in the manuscript.

all_original_sections.original_text:
## 1. Recommendation

**Recommendation at the requested four-journal benchmark: reject in the present form.**

Revision 111 contains genuine new mathematics and responds directly to one of the principal routes identified in the revision-110 report. It does not merely refine another scalar certificate, rename the persistent residual, or multiply a per-itinerary estimate by an uncontrolled number of collision words.

The revision proves three substantive results.

First, for a fixed lifted collision itinerary it proves global injectivity of the map

\[
Q\longmapsto (F(Q),\arg \nabla F(Q))
\]

on the noncritical regular physical trajectories, including trajectories lying in different connected components of the itinerary domain. The argument uses two convex support inequalities for the Cartesian broken-path length. It does not interpolate between the trajectories through a possibly forbidden physical path and does not assume that an angular word domain is convex.

Second, this roof--angle injectivity is combined with the retained stable-Jacobian pressure theorem and the optical comparison

\[
\omega\le C_0c_mJ^sT^m,
\qquad
\frac{J^sT}{c}\le C_1,
\]

to obtain a genuine target-roof physical word sum. For every prescribed set of distinct interior incidence marks \(S\), the revision proves

\[
\left\|
\frac{dF_\#\!\left(\prod_{i\in S}c_i^{-1}\mathbf1_\Pi\nu_R^*\right)}{dt}
\right\|_{L^\infty(dt)}
\le C_\star K_\star^{|S|},
\]

uniformly in the collision count, radius, original exact labels, roof, and marked indices. The proof reconstructs a full word from its unmarked blocks and at most \(|S|\) deleted physical step symbols, so adjacent marks and zero-length blocks are included. This is a weighted pressure sum, not a raw word count.

Third, the revision applies the marked theorem to the actual positive persistent source. It proves that persistent states carrying an incidence witness deeper than an explicit \(O(\log m)\) collision-end layer have zero \(m^2\)-normalized essential height, and that states carrying at least

\[
s_m\asymp \frac{\log m}{\log\log m}
\]

incidence witnesses also have zero normalized height. The witness may depend on the target roof and angle; no single witness is selected for a whole physical segment.

I audited the new modules

- `core/265_global_roof_angle_uniqueness.tex`;
- `core/266_target_roof_marked_pressure.tex`;
- `core/267_uniform_incidence_witness_summation.tex`;

as well as the active article, the revised local explanations in modules 262--263, the response, proof ledger, source manifest, publication-status flags, validation record, the controlling revision-110 report, and the source-pinned historical inputs needed by the new pressure argument.

Within the assumptions actually stated in those files, I found no decisive sign error in the support inequalities, no missing marked stable factor, no evident off-by-one error in the block decomposition, no uncontrolled physical-word multiplier, no invalid positive-source subtraction, no exponent error in the depth or factorial schedules, and no illegal substitution of a collision-dependent width into a theorem stated only at fixed width. The new target-roof summation chain is mathematically coherent relative to its inherited inputs.

The negative recommendation is nevertheless forced by the exact endpoint of the argument. The revised scalar theorem is

\[
\mathcal E_M
\le
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm loc})
+C_MB^{-1/384},
\]

where

\[
\mathsf R_B^{\rm loc}
=
\bigl(\mathsf U_B^{\rm loc}-K_BP_{r_B}^{\rm ng}\bigr)_+.
\]

The manuscript proves that the unchanged exact-label raw pointwise assertion is equivalent to

\[
\mathcal H_M(\mathsf R_B^{\rm loc})\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{for every fixed }M.
\]

**No theorem establishes this limit.**

The remaining source still permits:

- shallow incidence witnesses in the two logarithmic collision-end layers;
- fewer than \(s_m\) incidence witnesses, with no pointwise smallness obtained merely from that number bound;
- clearance witnesses at arbitrary depth, including tangencies to unvisited disks;
- critical entrances and section cuts not paid by the new incidence insertion;
- source on which the full nongrazing comparison pool remains capacity-deficient; and
- any singular endpoint or pairing configuration outside the inherited regular physical-source hypotheses.

The new marked-pressure bound is deliberately unscaled. Its all-incidence consequence is \(O(\varepsilon(B))\), not \(O(m^{-2})\). At fixed outer \(B\), multiplying that bound by \(m^2\) does not make it small. Only the additional depth and factorial factors pay the two classes isolated in revision 111.

Thus revision 111 proves a real target-roof weighted summation theorem and removes nontrivial portions of the persistent source in the correct topology, but the residual in equation `eq:v111-remaining` is still the upper pointwise obstruction itself. It is not a harmless remainder after the organizing local limit theorem.

At the requested benchmark, this is not sufficient for acceptance. A positive recommendation would require closure of the complete localized-shortage estimate, or a reformulation around a complete theorem of independent breadth and significance. Revision 111 supplies neither yet.
